title: Clean up parse_plan re-export from plan.py __all__
description: plan.py imports parse_plan from model and re-exports it in __all__, but no code imports parse_plan from dagshund.plan — __init__.py imports it directly from dagshund.model. The re-export is misleading since plan.py is now predicates and detection functions, not parsing. Remove parse_plan from plan.py's import and __all__.

title: Phantom nodes for serving_endpoint → registered_model when model absent from plan
description:
SERVING_ENDPOINT_MODEL_SPEC correctly traverses config.served_entities[].entity_name and creates a lateral edge to resources.registered_models.{name}. However, if the registered model is NOT in the plan, no phantom node is created — the target resolution returns empty.

The lateral-deps fixture exercises this: phantom_endpoint references dagshund.phantom_schema.phantom_model which exists in the workspace but not in the bundle.

Note: the plan.json nests served_entities under endpoint_details.config.served_entities, not config.served_entities directly. The extraction code (extractResourceState + getUnknownProp) may need adjustment for this nesting.

Needs:
- A phantom collector (or extension of an existing one) that scans model_serving_endpoints for entity_name references and creates registered-model::{name} phantoms when the model isn't in the plan
- Register registered-model:: as a leaf phantom prefix in isPhantomLeaf() if not already present
- Handle the endpoint_details.config nesting in extractResourceState
- Verify with: just gen-expected lateral-deps && just test-golden

title: add typed Zod schemas for PermissionsState and GrantsState
description: Sub-resource state shapes are treated as generic records. The CLI defines specific types: PermissionsState { object_id, permissions[] } and GrantsState { securable_type, full_name, grants[] }. Adding typed schemas would enable better rendering of sub-resource state in the detail panel (e.g., formatting permission entries as a table). Low priority since generic handling works.

title: Filter cannot search by type:task for individual task fields
description:
The --filter flag supports type:jobs, type:schemas, etc. to filter by resource type. But there's no way to filter by individual task fields within a job — e.g. show only task-level changes within a large job with 60+ task changes.

Resolved: added field:X token to the filter DSL. Substring matches against field change keys (e.g. field:email_notifications, field:task).

title: Document or mitigate debug trace leaking sensitive plan data
description: debug.py:34-60 — when --debug or DAGSHUND_DEBUG is set, the profile hook logs up to 80 chars of function arguments to stderr via _summarize_value. If plan JSON contains sensitive values (API keys, connection strings in Databricks resource state), these could leak to stderr and into CI build logs. Consider documenting this in --help output, or masking values that look like secrets.

title: Add raw JSON toggle button to detail panel
description: Add a toggle button to the detail panel that reveals the raw JSON of the changes/resourceState for the selected node. Useful for debugging and inspecting the exact plan output. Button should toggle between the formatted per-field view and a raw JSON view showing the underlying data.

title: Toggle to hide source-table phantom nodes
description: Add a toolbar toggle that hides source-table:: phantom leaf nodes and their edges from the UC tree. These nodes show spec.source_table_full_name references from synced_database_tables — useful for understanding data lineage but noisy when reviewing deployment diffs. Toggle should filter nodes out entirely (no empty space), not just dim them. Related to dagshund-czfs (broader lateral edge toggle) but distinct: this removes phantom nodes, not just edges between real nodes.

title: Split InteractionContext into hover and selection contexts
description: InteractionContext re-renders every node component on every hover change because hoveredNodeId is part of the context value. Split into a HoverContext (hoveredNodeId, connectedIds) and SelectionContext (selectedNodeId, selectedConnectedIds, filterMatchedIds, etc.) so hover changes only re-render hover-sensitive consumers. This would reduce the O(N) re-render cascade on hover and further improve click reliability on large graphs.
close_reason: won't-fix: all node components consume all InteractionContext fields via useNodeDimming, so splitting into hover/selection contexts wouldn't reduce re-renders. startTransition already handles the priority issue.

title: Add empty-string action handling to Python _ACTIONS dict
description: TypeScript actionTypeSchema includes empty string mapped to unchanged/skip. Python _ACTIONS dict has no entry for empty string — falls through to _DEFAULT_ACTION (unknown, ? prefix). A plan with action: empty string renders as unchanged in browser but unknown in terminal. Fix: add empty string entry to _ACTIONS.

title: Sub-resource keys render as independent nodes
description:
Databricks Asset Bundle plans use 4-segment keys for sub-resources: `resources.TYPE.NAME.SUBRESOURCE` (e.g. `resources.jobs.test_job.permissions`, `resources.jobs.test_job.run_as`). The codebase assumes exactly 3 segments (`resources.TYPE.NAME`), causing sub-resources to render as independent top-level nodes.

**Revised approach (v2):** Don't filter sub-resources out — fold them into their parent resource entry. Sub-resource data (permissions, run_as config, changes) must remain visible in the parent's detail panel.

**Merge strategy:**
- Sub-resource changes get prefixed into parent's changes as `subresource_name.field_name` (e.g. `permissions.permission_level`)
- Sub-resource remote_state folds into parent's resource state display
- Sub-resource depends_on pointing to parent is structural (drop)
- Sub-resource depends_on pointing to external resources becomes phantom nodes / lateral edges on the parent

**Reproducer:** `dagshund single_test/blub.json` — `test_job.permissions` previously appeared as a separate job. After v1 fix it was filtered out entirely, losing permission data from the detail panel.

**Scope:** Both TS (HTML DAG) and Python (text CLI). The `isSubResourceKey` predicate from v1 is reused to identify sub-resources, but instead of filtering them out, they get merged into their parent before graph building.

title: Move diff-state-styles test to tests/utils/
description: diff-state-styles.ts moved from components/ to utils/ but its test file remains at tests/components/diff-state-styles.test.ts. Move to tests/utils/diff-state-styles.test.ts to match.

title: Enforce naming conventions across codebase
description: Rename abbreviated variables (rt, ctx, cfg, pg*, s*), single-letter callbacks, vague function names (runBuild, readDistAssets, runLateralEdgeSpec, entryEdgeDiffState), boolean (wrapFlat), type (ElkLayoutResult), file renames (App.tsx, compute-search-matched-ids.test.ts), and detail-panel handleKeyDown.

title: CI: run quality gate on every push
description:
The quality gate (lint + typecheck + test) only runs on tag pushes (v*.*.*) in .gitlab-ci.yml. Regular pushes to main only get SAST/secret scanning. This means a regression can merge and sit undetected until a release is cut.

Fix: change the quality stage rules to run on every push (or at minimum every push to main), not just tags. The tag-only gate should remain for publish, but quality should run earlier.

title: expand dangerous actions to include PostgreSQL resource types
description:
Currently _STATEFUL_RESOURCE_WARNINGS only covers Unity Catalog types: catalogs, schemas, volumes, registered_models. PostgreSQL-related resource types (database_instances, database_catalogs) and other stateful types need warnings too.

Candidates to add:
- database_instances — dropping a PostgreSQL instance destroys all databases and data
- database_catalogs — dropping a catalog loses all objects within it
- experiments — MLflow experiment data and runs would be lost
- quality_monitors — monitoring history and metrics would be lost
- secret_scopes — all secrets in the scope would be lost

Related to dagshund-1ssh (expand stateful resource warnings beyond 4 types) but specifically focused on PostgreSQL resources which are particularly dangerous since they hold user data.

title: expand stateful resource warnings beyond 4 types
description: Only catalogs, schemas, volumes, registered_models have data-loss warnings on delete/recreate. Other potentially stateful types — database_instances, database_catalogs, experiments, quality_monitors, secret_scopes — have no warnings. Need to research which types are actually stateful and expand _STATEFUL_RESOURCE_WARNINGS accordingly.

title: graph: place Lakebase Postgres catalogs meaningfully
description:
During dagshund-3l7p Lakebase fixture work, the new resources.postgres_catalogs.dev_catalog entry rendered under Workspace -> Other Resources. That is current code behavior because js/src/graph/build-resource-graph.ts classifies only postgres_projects, postgres_branches, and postgres_endpoints as POSTGRES_TYPES, while UC catalog-tier handling includes catalogs and database_catalogs but not postgres_catalogs.

Fixture context:

    resources.postgres_catalogs.dev_catalog:
      action: create
      new_state:
        value:
          branch: "${resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id}"
          catalog_id: dagshund_lakebase
          postgres_database: dagshund_lakebase
          create_database_if_missing: true
        vars:
          branch: "${resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id}"

This resource is ambiguous visually:
- It is visible to users as a Unity Catalog catalog named dagshund_lakebase.
- It is deployed into / bound to a Lakebase Postgres branch, in this fixture the dev branch.

Investigate and choose the graph model deliberately. Possible directions:
- Treat postgres_catalogs as a Postgres/Lakebase child of the branch, because its semantic branch field points at resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id.
- Treat it as a UC catalog node, because users see it in Unity Catalog, possibly with a lateral edge to the Lakebase branch.
- Represent both relationships if the graph can do so without clutter: primary placement in one hierarchy plus a lateral edge to the other.

Do not blindly use depends_on. If using the branch relationship, resolve the semantic branch field, including bundle refs like "${resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id}". Coordinate with dagshund-pz00, which tracks resolving Lakebase endpoint parent refs from semantic parent fields.

Acceptance criteria:
- postgres_catalogs no longer appears as an unexplained flat Other Resources node in the Lakebase fixture.
- The chosen placement is documented in docs/guidelines/VISUALIZATION.md.
- Focused JS tests cover the chosen behavior using a postgres_catalogs entry bound to a branch resource ref.
- Existing database_catalogs UC behavior remains unchanged unless intentionally redesigned.
close_reason: done: delivered in completed Lakebase fixture and graph work

title: Add hook-level tests for usePhantomLeafState
description: Add tests for usePhantomLeafState hook with a small graph fixture that exercises cascade pruning: phantom leaf hidden -> parent phantom with no remaining visible children also hidden -> edges touching hidden nodes removed. Pure isPhantomLeaf is already tested; this covers the cascade algorithm. Could test via renderHook with mock Node/Edge arrays.

title: Always show added/modified/removed filter buttons in toolbar
description:
The DiffFilterToolbar hides Added/Modified/Removed buttons when their count is 0. This looks odd when the lateral edge / phantom leaf toggles (which have similar conditional logic) render next to them — the toolbar reflows inconsistently.

Fix: always render Added/Modified/Removed buttons even with count 0. Keep the hide-when-empty behavior for the rare Unknown state.

Location: js/src/components/diff-filter-toolbar.tsx

title: README refresh after CLI flag audit

After the flag audit (dagshund-3ecq) lands, do a single pass over README.md to fix inaccuracies, improve descriptions, and ensure all examples reflect the final flag names and behavior. Check EPILOG and SKILL.md for consistency too.

title: flatParentId duplication
description: flatParentId condition (workspaceEntries.length > 0 && postgresEntries.length > 0) is computed independently in both buildWorkspaceGraph and buildResourceGraph. If workspace wrapping logic changes, the copy in buildResourceGraph could drift. Fix: return flatParentId from buildWorkspaceGraph or extract a shared helper.

title: Protect GitLab release environments post first deploy
description: After the first successful tag pipeline creates the release and release-test environments in GitLab, protect them: Settings → CI/CD → Environments → edit each one → enable 'Protect this environment' → restrict deployment to Maintainers only. This prevents anyone with push access from triggering PyPI publishes without maintainer role.
close_reason: Protected environments require GitLab Premium. Existing controls sufficient: protected tags (Maintainers only), manual publish gates, OIDC environment claims verified on PyPI side.

title: debug.py: surface exceptions, add indent-by-depth
description:
The `-d` / `enable_profile_tracing` mode is the right shape for bug reports from users (one flag, redirect stderr, email the file). Keep the feature. Two narrow bugs to fix:

1. **Exceptions vanish from the trace.** `sys.setprofile` fires `event='return'` with `arg=None` when a frame exits via exception. Current output renders this as `← parse_plan → None (12.3ms)` — indistinguishable from a clean return. Fix: detect exception exits (check `sys.exc_info()` in the return branch, or switch to `sys.settrace` which fires `'exception'` events) and mark them explicitly in the log line, e.g. `✗ parse_plan raised DagshundError (12.3ms)`.

2. **No indentation → call tree shape invisible.** `len(call_stack)` is already tracked; use it as an indent prefix so nested calls show their depth:
   ```
   → parse_plan(raw=str(1823) '...')
     → parse_plan_data(raw=dict(4 keys))
       → parse_resource_change(key='resources.jobs.etl', ...)
   ```

Out of scope for this bead: the performance cost on very large plans (`_summarize_value` on every arg, every call). Note it in `--help` or leave it — bug reports are the use case and slow-but-readable is fine.

~10 lines of change. Not a rewrite.

title: epic: Staff Review R3 — Architecture, Code Quality, UX, Security
description: Third staff review round with 4 expert reviewers (architect, code quality, UX, security/perf). 29 actionable findings across HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW priorities. All findings cross-referenced against 119 closed beads to confirm novelty.

title: Stdin pipe input: accept plan JSON and open browser
description:
Accept databricks bundle plan JSON via stdin pipe and serve the webview.

USAGE PATTERN:
  databricks bundle plan -o json | dagshund
  # or from a file:
  cat plan.json | dagshund

WHAT EXISTS:
- src/index.ts — Bun server entry point (currently just serves static HTML)
- parsePlanFromString in parser/ — validates JSON string into Plan

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. Detect stdin pipe in src/index.ts — if process.stdin is not a TTY, read all stdin to string
2. Parse the stdin JSON using parsePlanFromString
3. Inject the parsed plan into the served HTML as a script tag: window.__DAGSHUND_PLAN__ = <json>
4. Auto-open the browser after server starts (use Bun.spawn or child_process to open localhost URL)
5. Frontend (src/frontend.tsx or App.tsx) reads window.__DAGSHUND_PLAN__ on mount and feeds it to the graph

FALLBACK: If no stdin, serve the app anyway with empty state (for dev mode / future file upload)

DATA CONTEXT:
- Plan JSON can be large (hundreds of resources with nested tasks and changes records)
- The window.__DAGSHUND_PLAN__ global holds the raw parsed Plan object
- The rendering layer (dagshund-qu9) reads this and passes it through the graph model

CONSTRAINTS:
- Handle parse errors gracefully — print to stderr and exit with code 1
- Use Result type from types/result.ts
- No global mutable state — read stdin once, inject into HTML response
- Server should pick an available port if default is taken (nice to have, not blocking)
close_reason: Stdin pipe input implemented: server reads stdin, parses with Zod, serves at /api/plan. Frontend fetches dynamically with loading/empty/error/ready states. Auto-opens browser on pipe.

title: Refactor _render_field_change into smaller composable functions
description: _render_field_change in text.py is 46 lines with 6 distinct rendering branches (drift, no-op, remote-only, long-string, normal, empty). Each branch could be a focused helper function to stay under the 20-line guideline. Discovered during dagshund-27ah review.

title: fitView uses single rAF — may race with ResizeObserver
description: The initial fitView effect in flow-canvas.tsx (line ~173) uses a single requestAnimationFrame, but React Flow's ResizeObserver may not have measured node dimensions yet. The focusNodeId effect already handles this correctly with setTimeout(50ms). In HTML export mode the plan loads synchronously (no network delay), making the race more likely. Only reproduces on the Jobs tab — job group nodes require multiple ResizeObserver cycles (measure children, then resize parent container), widening the race window vs flat resource nodes. Fix: match the focusNodeId pattern — use setTimeout inside the rAF, or double-rAF.

title: investigate raw JSON expand field shows pre-merge or post-merge data
description: The detail panel has a raw JSON expand section at the bottom. Need to verify whether it shows the original PlanEntry (pre-merge, with sub-resource keys separate) or the merged PlanEntry (post-merge, with sub-resource data injected). If it shows pre-merge data, sub-resource state won't be visible there. If post-merge, it should include the injected permissions/grants state and prefixed changes. Check what data flows into the raw JSON component and whether it matches what users expect to see.

title: CI: Playwright smoke test for browser output
description:
Implement the Playwright browser smoke layer designed in dagshund-ibln.

## Scope

### 1. Playwright harness
- Install Playwright in js/ as dev dependency (pin Chromium version)
- Test suite js/tests/browser/smoke.spec.ts covering 3 fixtures:
  - mixed-changes (rich diff rendering)
  - all-hierarchies (layout stress test)
  - no-changes (empty-state rendering)
- Assertions per fixture:
  - No JS errors logged to console
  - React Flow node count > 0 (select via [data-testid] or role)
  - Diff badges present on diff-bearing fixtures
- NO screenshot diffing (too flaky for this layer; future bead if needed)

### 2. CI jobs
- build-template (new): bun run --cwd js build:template. Runs on feature branch push + MR. Artifact: the built template HTML.
- browser (new): needs build-template + quality. MR-only (\$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == \"merge_request_event\"). Runs Playwright suite against built template.
- Image: dedicated Playwright image with pinned version — NEVER :latest. Pick a specific mcr.microsoft.com/playwright tag at implementation time.
- interruptible: true

### 3. Local target
- Add just test-browser — builds template + runs Playwright suite locally
- NOT included in just check (keeps check fast)

### 4. Docs
- Update .claude/WORKFLOW.md \"Browser verification\" step to mention just test-browser as automated alternative to manual just dev

## Out of scope (covered elsewhere)
- Golden graph/text/exit/filter checks → dagshund-39ue
- Pipeline workflow rules, caching, interruptible on other jobs → dagshund-39ue (must land first as the CI shell)
- Screenshot regression testing → future bead if needed

## Dependency
This bead REQUIRES dagshund-39ue to have landed the workflow-rules shell (MR-then-branch, docs/beads skip, caching) so the browser job drops into a coherent pipeline structure.

## Acceptance
- just test-browser runs green locally
- MR pipeline includes build-template + browser jobs, both pass on the 3 fixtures
- browser job total duration ≤ 2 min after caching warms
- Playwright image tag is pinned (not :latest) in .gitlab-ci.yml
close_reason: Closing as won't-pursue. The golden fixture + graph-extractor + CI tier shipped in be8b53c already covers regression detection for DAG structure (expected-graph.json compared via extract-graph.ts) and terminal/markdown output (expected.txt/.md diffing). Playwright's marginal value over that is just 'does the bundled HTML actually render' — worth revisiting only if we see regressions that slip past the graph-level checks.

title: canvas: zoom in/out buttons in bottom-right panel
description:
## Observed

The bottom-right canvas panel currently has a single \"Fit view\" button (\`flow-canvas-layout.tsx:131-154\`). No zoom in / zoom out controls. Users must rely on the trackpad, Ctrl+scroll, or pinch gesture — which is unreliable on a mouse-only setup and non-obvious to discover.

## Proposal

Add two buttons (\`+\` / \`−\`) next to the existing fit-view button, calling React Flow's native \`zoomIn()\` / \`zoomOut()\` instance methods. Stacked or inline — whichever reads better visually.

## Scope (~30 LOC)

- \`js/src/hooks/use-viewport-positioning.ts\` — add \`handleZoomIn\` / \`handleZoomOut\` callbacks mirroring the existing \`handleFitView\` pattern. Both call the same \`rfInstanceRef.current?.zoomIn()\` / \`.zoomOut()\`.
- \`js/src/components/flow-canvas.tsx\` — destructure the two new handlers from \`useViewportPositioning\` and pass them down to \`FlowCanvasLayout\`.
- \`js/src/components/flow-canvas-layout.tsx\` — add two buttons in the existing \`<Panel position=\"bottom-right\">\`, reuse the same styling as the fit-view button. Native \`title=\` tooltips (\"Zoom in\" / \"Zoom out\") for consistency with dagshund-rkqa.
- Tests: none required — trivial forwarding onto React Flow's own API. Optional: a single render test asserting the two new buttons are in the DOM.

## Out of scope

- Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl++/Ctrl+-) — separate bead if desired
- Zoom-to-selection (zoom the viewport to a selected node bounding box)
- A zoom-level readout — the existing minimap is out of scope too; just the two buttons

## Discovered from

Spotted while hover-checking dagshund-rkqa badge tooltips — user noted the canvas has no discoverable zoom control.

title: fix: preserve graph state on tab switch (hide vs unmount)

This fully unmounts the inactive tab, losing all state (viewport position, selected node, hover state, filter state) and re-running expensive ELK layout on switch-back. title: CLI does not surface entity re-adds when remote topology drifts
description:
## Problem

When a nested resource (e.g. a job task, a schema grant) exists in the bundle but was manually deleted from the remote, bundle-apply will recreate it — but neither the CLI nor the browser detail panel surfaces this. Only the browser graph view catches it via topology comparison.

The same bug has a second face: the "Manual Edits Detected" footer counter undercounts and mislabels, because it only sees field-level overwrites and silently drops every topology-drift sub-entity (re-added and drift-removed).

## Reproduction

Fixture: `fixtures/golden/manual-drift/plan.json`

### Case 1 — re-added task (tasks collection)

`drift_pipeline.changes.tasks[task_key='transform']`:

- `remote_state.tasks` has 2 tasks: `ingest`, `publish`
- `new_state.tasks` has 3 tasks: `ingest`, `publish`, `transform`
- Bundle-apply will recreate `transform` on the remote

Databricks encodes this as:
```json
"tasks[task_key='transform']": {
  "action": "update",
  "old": {...full transform task...},
  "new": {...identical transform task...}
}
```

Note: `old == new`, no `remote` field.

### Case 2 — re-added grant (grants collection)

`drift_grants.grants.changes.[principal='data_engineers']`:

- `remote_state` grants list has only `data_readers`
- `new_state` grants list has `data_engineers` + `data_readers`
- Bundle-apply will recreate the `data_engineers` grant

Databricks encodes this as:
```json
"[principal='data_engineers']": {
  "action": "update",
  "old": {...full data_engineers grant...},
  "new": {...identical grant...}
}
```

Same shape as Case 1: `old == new`, no `remote` field, inside a parent whose `action` is `update`.

### Why two cases matter

Two completely different resource types (`jobs.tasks[]` and `schemas.grants[].[principal]`) exhibit the exact same encoding. That proves the detection rule is generic — "whole-entity no-op inside an update context with no `remote` field" — not something to hardcode per collection type. A single pre-pass over `changes` handles both.

### Current CLI behavior

The field-by-field renderer sees each of these as a no-op (old == new, no remote) and suppresses them entirely. `expected.txt` does not mention `transform` being re-added nor `data_engineers` grant being re-added anywhere. The only signal surfaces in the browser graph view, which derives edges from `new_state` vs `remote_state` topology directly.

## Manual Edits Detected footer is undercounting and mislabeling

Current footer output for `fixtures/golden/manual-drift/plan.json`:

```
Manual Edits Detected:
⚠ jobs/drift_pipeline was edited outside the bundle (2 fields will be overwritten)
⚠ schemas/drift_grants was edited outside the bundle (1 field will be overwritten)
```

What actually happened per plan.json:

**drift_pipeline** — 3 remote discrepancies, not 2:
1. `edit_mode`: remote `EDITABLE`, bundle wants `UI_LOCKED` — **overwritten**
2. `tasks[publish].depends_on[0].task_key`: remote `ingest`, bundle wants `transform` — **overwritten**
3. `tasks[transform]`: entire task missing from remote, bundle will **re-add** it

**drift_grants** — 2 remote discrepancies, not 1:
1. `grants.[data_readers].privileges`: remote `[USE_SCHEMA]`, bundle wants `[SELECT, USE_SCHEMA]` — **overwritten** (partial)
2. `grants.[data_engineers]`: entire grant missing from remote, bundle will **re-add** it

Two problems with the footer:

1. **Undercount.** Topology-drift entities (re-adds and drift-removes) aren't counted at all, because the footer walks the same suppressed field list as the per-resource renderer.
2. **Mislabeling.** Every remote discrepancy is described as "will be overwritten". That's only true for field-level drift. Whole-entity topology drift is either **re-added** (missing from remote → bundle recreates) or **drift-removed** (present in remote → bundle deletes on apply). These need distinct labels, not a lumped "overwritten" count.

A correct footer would look something like:

```
Manual Edits Detected:
⚠ jobs/drift_pipeline was edited outside the bundle
    2 fields will be overwritten
    1 task will be re-added (transform)
⚠ schemas/drift_grants was edited outside the bundle
    1 field will be overwritten
    1 grant will be re-added (data_engineers)
```

The counter and the per-resource renderer share the same underlying data: fix them together in a single pre-pass.

## Why the graph view catches it

`js/src/graph/...` derives nodes/edges from `new_state` vs `remote_state` topology directly, so it sees the `transform` entity missing from remote and renders it as added (green edge `transform->ingest`). This is the ONLY surface that tells the user transform is being re-added. The browser detail panel and the Python CLI both miss it.

## Fix direction

The CLI's field-renderer needs a pre-pass that walks the `changes` block and categorizes each entry by drift shape:

- **Field overwrite** (old == new, `remote` present and different) → current 15f7 rendering
- **Field drift with remote-only value** (action=update, only `remote` present) → current 15f7 rendering
- **Topology re-add** (old == new, no `remote`, inside an update-context parent) → NEW: emit `+ tasks[task_key='transform'] (re-added from drift)` / `+ grants.[principal='data_engineers'] (re-added from drift)` synthetic lines
- **Topology drift-remove** (entity in remote but not in new — if Databricks surfaces this at all) → NEW: emit `- tasks[...] (drift-removed)` synthetic lines

Same pre-pass feeds the "Manual Edits Detected" footer so both surfaces stay consistent. Footer should report three numbers per resource: `overwritten`, `re-added`, `drift-removed` — not a single lumped "fields".

Likely location: `src/dagshund/format.py`, wherever per-resource changes are rendered and wherever the footer summary is built.

Detection generic across collection types: key off the bracket-path shape already used by Databricks (`[key='value']` or `[task_key='...']`) rather than hardcoding per resource kind. Cases 1 and 2 above prove this works.

Golden fixture update for `manual-drift/expected.txt` and `expected.md` needed after the fix.

## Relationship to other issues

- **dagshund-15f7** (closed, on this branch): fixed browser remote-only/drift rendering — foundation this extends to the CLI surface
- **dagshund-17pi** (in progress, on this branch): browser isDrift flag for the same topology-drift cases — parallel work, different surface
- **dagshund-1m8f** (open, fixture improvement): `by_diff_state` counts in `expected-graph.json` — regression safety net for both 17pi and this bead

## Out of scope

- Making the graph view the source of truth (big refactor)
- Changing what Databricks emits in plan.json (upstream)
- Detecting whole-resource drift where the entire top-level resource is missing from the remote — Databricks collapses that to `action: create` with no `remote_state`, undetectable from plan.json alone (see \`drift_doomed\` in the manual-drift fixture). This bead is strictly for sub-entity topology drift inside an update-context parent.

## Discovered during

Manual verification of dagshund-15f7 on \`fixtures/golden/manual-drift/plan.json\`. User asked why graph shows green edge but CLI/detail panel don't mention transform being re-added. Strengthened during dagshund-17pi fixture extension when the new grants case surfaced the same shape in a second resource type and exposed the footer counter bug.

title: Reconsider dict/list summarization in field change display
description:
format_value() in format.py summarizes dicts as '{N fields}' and lists as '[N items]' — e.g. 'email_notifications: {1 fields} (remote)'. This hides the actual content, which may be more useful to show inline or expanded.

Current approach (in progress): inline small collections using human-readable format (unquoted keys, spaces). Falls back to {N fields}/[N items] when rendered string exceeds 60 chars.

Also: the README needs clear documentation of what (remote) and (drift) mean in the output:
- (remote): field exists on the server but is not managed by the bundle. Deploy won't touch it. Purely informational.
- (drift): server value differs from what the bundle expects. Deploy will overwrite the server value back to the bundle's value.

title: Discuss CLI flag structure for output modes
description: Current flag structure: -o controls HTML file output, --format controls stdout format (text/md), -e controls exit codes. These compose: '-o out.html --format md -e' produces all three outputs. Question: is this the right UX? Alternatives to consider: (1) should --format also accept 'html' and replace -o? (2) should -o accept format hints like '-o report.md'? (3) is the implicit 'no stdout when -o without --format' behavior clear enough? (4) should --format default to md when -o is set, since the common CI case is both?

title: Clicking nodes sometimes fails to open detail panel

May be related to the existing drag-vs-click disambiguation issue (see won't-fix: 50ms symmetric debounce). Needs investigation to determine if this is the same root cause or a separate bug.

title: ELK singleton never recovers from Worker failure
description:
layout-graph.ts:24-32 — getElk() caches a single ELK instance (backed by a Web Worker) forever. If the Worker dies (OOM, crash), every subsequent layout call rejects permanently. The UI shows 'Layout failed' with no recovery path except page refresh.

Investigation (2026-03-14): Deployment plan DAGs are small (tens to low hundreds of nodes) — not enough to OOM a Worker. Page refresh is an acceptable recovery for the unlikely crash case. Closing as won't-fix.

title: display unresolved variable references from new_state.vars
description: Changes can have 'old', 'new', AND 'remote' fields. Usually remote === old, but they diverge when someone edited the resource outside the bundle (manual drift). We could detect remote != old and surface a warning in both text and browser output. Could be feature creep — the CLI already handles drift by using remote as the baseline. Evaluate whether the visual indicator adds value or just noise.

title: Browser: array reorder shows confusing identical old/new values
description:
When Databricks reorders an array (e.g. job_clusters) without changing values, the plan reports positional updates with old == new but different remote. Dagshund renders these as confusing identical -/+ lines.

If we detect that an array is just reordered (same elements at different positions, no actual value changes), the whole array should collapse to unchanged — no modified entries at all.

Additional inconsistency in the plan data: some drift fields include old/new (showing confusing identical -/+ lines without '(vs remote)' label), while others only include remote (correctly showing '(vs remote)' label). When old/new are present and identical, the structural diff should detect drift (old == new, remote differs) and show the '(vs remote)' label instead of identical -/+ lines.

In the CLI, drift-only fields (only remote, no old/new) show the field name with no value at all — e.g. 'job_clusters[1].new_cluster.num_workers' with nothing after it. This is confusing because there's no context about what changed or what the remote value is.

Two sub-problems:
1. Detect array reorder (all elements present in both old and new, just different positions) and suppress the noise
2. Detect drift in individual fields (old == new with different remote) and render as '(vs remote)' instead of identical -/+ lines — both in browser UI and CLI. For CLI drift-only fields (no old/new, only remote), show the remote value.

Affects both browser UI and Python CLI.

title: bump: ty 0.0.23 -> 0.0.31
description:
Bump ty (dev dep in pyproject.toml) from 0.0.23 -> 0.0.31.

## Why separate from the patch bundle
ty is pre-1.0 and moves fast — 8 patches behind. Known to have breaking diagnostic changes between releases. Risk of surfacing new errors that need triage. Keep the bump mechanical and isolated so any diagnostic noise is obviously attributable.

## Steps
1. Bump ty==0.0.31 in pyproject.toml dev group
2. uv sync
3. just typecheck-py — review any new diagnostics
4. If new errors: either fix or file follow-up beads (do not silence)
5. just check

## Reference
Memory note: 'ty moves fast and has known incompatibilities; pin carefully' — part of why the version-audit bead (dagshund-2omy) called this one out specifically.

title: Phantom UC nodes for synced table source_table_full_name references

title: add HTML provenance information panel
description:
Add an accessible provenance information button to the top-right application controls beside the light/dark and high-contrast buttons. Activating it opens a compact panel describing the self-contained HTML artifact and the exact source plan consumed by Dagshund.

Required displayed provenance, in this order:
1. Source plan: the source file basename when Dagshund was invoked with a positional file, or stdin when input was piped.
2. Last modified: the source file mtime rendered as a UTC ISO 8601 timestamp, or unknown for stdin. This is explicitly modification time, not creation time or ctime.
3. Source plan SHA-256: lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the exact raw input bytes.
4. Dagshund version: the version that generated the HTML.
5. Databricks CLI version (plan metadata): the top-level cli_version from the parsed input plan, or unknown when absent.

Input and hashing contract:
- Keep both existing invocation paths working: dagshund PLAN.json -o report.html and cat PLAN.json | dagshund -o report.html.
- Change the shared CLI input boundary to read bytes, not text. File input must use a binary file handle. Stdin input must use sys.stdin.buffer. Do not reread either source.
- For file input, derive only Path(plan_file).name and obtain st_mtime from os.fstat on the same open file descriptor used to read the bytes. Never embed the full or resolved input path.
- For stdin, record source_name as stdin and source_modified_at as null. A pipe has no portable filename or filesystem timestamp.
- Decode the consumed bytes as UTF-8 for the existing JSON parser and preserve current domain-specific invalid-UTF-8 errors for file input; add an explicit DagshundError for invalid UTF-8 on stdin.
- Calculate hashlib.sha256(raw_bytes).hexdigest() only when HTML output is requested. Calculate it before decoding, parsing, secret redaction, normalization, or JSON reserialization.
- Use the same byte-oriented reader for terminal, Markdown, and HTML modes so ingestion behavior cannot diverge. Non-HTML modes do not calculate or render provenance.
- Do not hash plan.raw, decoded text re-encoded as UTF-8, redacted data, normalized data, or the compact JSON embedded in HTML. Those representations are not the exact source bytes.
- Do not retain source bytes in the Plan domain model. Keep source identity at the CLI/browser export boundary and release the byte buffer after hashing and UTF-8 decoding.

Python metadata and HTML boundary:
- Add a frozen, slotted data carrier for HTML provenance with explicit fields for source basename, nullable source mtime, source SHA-256, Dagshund version, and nullable plan CLI version. Follow PYTHON.md naming and typing rules.
- Build the provenance object from the source descriptor, exact-byte digest, dagshund.__version__, and Plan.cli_version.
- Extend browser rendering to inject provenance as compact JSON alongside the existing redacted plan JSON. Keep the generated HTML self-contained, offline, and protected by the existing CSP and script-tag escaping.
- Define a dedicated embedded metadata global such as window.__DAGSHUND_PROVENANCE__. Do not add provenance fields to the raw plan object and do not scrape rendered text.
- Validate every template placeholder exactly once before substitution. Perform substitution so placeholder-like strings in plan values, provenance values, or filenames cannot be interpreted as template slots.
- Embed only the basename, mtime, digest, Dagshund version, and plan CLI version. Do not expose the source path, original bytes, additional raw plan fields, or unredacted values.
- Keep UC secret redaction and the existing window.__DAGSHUND_PLAN__ transport unchanged apart from the necessary template assembly plumbing.

TypeScript boundary:
- Add a dedicated Zod schema and inferred readonly type for provenance. Use zod/v4, readonly objects, z.unknown at the global boundary, and the existing Result style for validation failures.
- Generated provenance has required source_name, nullable source_modified_at, 64-character lowercase hexadecimal source_plan_sha256, dagshund_version, and nullable plan_cli_version fields.
- Treat an absent embedded provenance global as missing metadata rather than failing plan loading. This supports the development server and explicit missing-metadata component coverage.
- Keep provenance parsing separate from plan parsing. The graph and Plan domain types must not depend on provenance.

Top-right UI and accessibility:
- Render one provenance control from App in the existing absolute top-right control group. It must not be placed in SearchBar or duplicated per graph tab.
- Place an icon-only information button adjacent to ThemeToggle. Give it an accessible name, aria-expanded, aria-controls, a tooltip/title, and the same visible focus-ring treatment as the theme controls.
- Open a compact, visually secondary non-modal popover or dialog that stays outside graph interaction space and works in light, dark, and high-contrast themes.
- Render rows in the required order. Use a monospace, wrapping or breakable presentation for the SHA-256 so it cannot overflow.
- Render nullable plan CLI version and source mtime as unknown. When all embedded provenance is absent, render unknown values rather than crashing.
- Native button keyboard activation must work. Escape closes the panel, an explicit accessible close button closes it, outside click closes it, and focus returns to the information button after close. Opening should move focus to a useful element in the panel.

Python verification:
- Update tests for the byte-oriented file and stdin readers, including invalid UTF-8 behavior.
- Prove exact-byte hashing with inputs whose parsed JSON is equivalent but whose bytes differ through whitespace and CRLF line endings. Expected values must be computed from the original bytes, not from normalized text.
- Cover file basename extraction, no full-path leakage, controlled file mtime conversion to UTC ISO 8601, and stdin source_name/unknown mtime behavior.
- Cover metadata generation with present and absent cli_version and the current Dagshund version.
- Cover provenance template injection, placeholder cardinality, script-tag escaping, compact JSON, existing secret redaction, and an input value or basename containing placeholder-like text.
- Cover both CLI HTML paths: positional file output embeds filename and mtime; stdin output embeds stdin, null mtime, and the exact stdin digest.
- Preserve existing terminal and Markdown behavior and tests.

TypeScript verification:
- Add focused schema/parser tests for present metadata, nullable values, a missing global, malformed metadata, and invalid SHA-256 shape.
- Add component tests for present provenance values, unknown rendering, field order, icon-button accessible name, aria-expanded, keyboard activation, explicit close, Escape close, outside-click close, and focus return.
- Update HTML assembler tests for the dedicated provenance placeholder/global and safe embedding.
- Do not test React or Zod internals.

Generated artifact and completion gates:
- Do not hand-edit src/dagshund/_assets/template.html. Regenerate it through nix develop --command just build after source changes.
- Run nix develop --command just check.
- Run nix develop --command just build and verify the wheel contains the regenerated self-contained template.
- Browser verification must cover both development rendering with missing provenance and an actual generated HTML file with present file provenance. Verify light, dark, high contrast, keyboard open/close, Escape, explicit close, focus visibility, SHA wrapping, and that graph pan/zoom remains unaffected.
- Follow the required three-pass review and approval workflow before committing.

Acceptance:
A saved HTML file generated from a positional plan file identifies the source basename, source mtime, exact source-byte SHA-256, Dagshund generator version, and plan CLI version without network access. An HTML file generated from stdin identifies the source as stdin, shows Last modified as unknown, and still identifies the exact piped bytes by SHA-256. Terminal and Markdown-only invocations retain their current output and avoid provenance hashing.

Dependency context:
The dependency refresh dagshund-ezp5 is complete.

title: Deduplicate graph building redundancies (#1-#6)
description:
Six concrete redundancies found in js/src/ graph building pipeline. All are straightforward extractions — no design decisions needed.

## 1. Extract useAsyncLayout hook (usePlanGraph / useResourceGraph)

**Files:** use-plan-graph.ts, use-resource-graph.ts
**Problem:** Both hooks are ~25 lines of identical async-state-management boilerplate. They manage loading/ready/error state, a cancellation flag, and error message extraction. The only difference is one expression — the layout function called inside the effect.

**usePlanGraph calls:** toReactFlowElements(buildPlanGraph(plan))
**useResourceGraph calls:** layoutResourceGraph(buildResourceGraph(plan))

**Fix:** Extract a useAsyncLayout(plan, transformFn) hook that accepts (plan: Plan) => Promise<LayoutResult>. Both hooks become one-line wrappers. Saves ~25 duplicated lines of state management, cancellation, and error handling.

## 2. Unify three parallel GraphEdge builders

**Files:** build-plan-graph.ts (buildDepEdge), build-resource-graph.ts (buildEdge), extract-lateral-edges.ts (buildLateralEdge)
**Problem:** Three separate functions construct GraphEdge objects with the same shape { id, source, target, label: undefined, diffState }. Each adds a minor twist:
- buildDepEdge: computes source/target from parts via buildTaskNodeId, no guard
- buildEdge: adds self-loop guard (returns undefined if source === target)
- buildLateralEdge: prefixes id with "lateral::"

**Fix:** Single buildGraphEdge(source, target, diffState?, options?) factory. Options could include { idPrefix?: string, allowSelfLoop?: boolean }. Or simpler: just buildGraphEdge(source, target, diffState?) as the base, with the self-loop guard applied at the call site (it's one line). The lateral prefix can be the idPrefix option.

## 3. Extract classifyChange helper (isTaskAdded/isTaskRemoved reimplemented 3x)

**Files:** resolve-task-diff-state.ts, build-plan-graph.ts, extract-tasks.ts
**Problem:** The logic "has new but not old → added / has old but not new → removed" is written three different ways:
- resolve-task-diff-state.ts: explicit isTaskAdded/isTaskRemoved helpers (check change.new/change.old)
- build-plan-graph.ts: inlined in resolveTaskEdgeDiffState (same checks, returns "added"/"removed"/undefined)
- extract-tasks.ts: inlined in extractDeletedTaskEntries (inverted check: skip if hasNew or no old)

**Fix:** Export a classifyChange(change: ChangeDesc): "added" | "removed" | "modified" | undefined from a shared location (resolve-task-diff-state.ts is a natural home, or a new utils/classify-change.ts). All three sites use it instead of reimplementing the same boolean logic.

## 4. Extract shared job node fields (buildJobNode / buildResourceNode overlap)

**Files:** build-plan-graph.ts (buildJobNode), build-resource-graph.ts (buildResourceNode, isJobEntry branch)
**Problem:** When building a node for a job resource, both functions compute identical fields:
- label: extractResourceName(key)
- diffState: mapActionToDiffState(entry.action)
- changes: filterJobLevelChanges(entry.changes)
- resourceState: resolveJobState(entry.new_state, entry.remote_state)
- taskChangeSummary: buildTaskChangeSummary(tasks, entry.action, entry.changes)

The only difference is nodeKind ("job" vs "resource") and how tasks are obtained (parameter vs inline resolveTaskEntries call).

**Fix:** Extract buildJobFields(key: string, entry: PlanEntry, tasks: readonly TaskEntry[]) that returns the shared field object. Each call site spreads it with its own nodeKind. Saves ~10 duplicated lines and ensures the two views stay in sync if job node logic changes.

## 5. Extract resolveAllTaskEntries helper (3-line pattern repeated twice)

**File:** build-plan-graph.ts (two locations: buildEntryGraph ~line 198 and buildRunJobEdges ~line 245)
**Problem:** The same 3-line sequence appears twice in the same file:
  const tasks = resolveTaskEntries(entry.new_state, entry.remote_state);
  const deletedTasks = extractDeletedTaskEntries(entry.changes);
  const allTasks = [...tasks, ...deletedTasks];

**Fix:** Extract resolveAllTaskEntries(entry: PlanEntry): readonly TaskEntry[] that combines live + deleted tasks in one call. Both call sites become one line.

## 6. Use existing toEdgeDiffState instead of inline reimplementation

**File:** build-plan-graph.ts lines 182-184
**Problem:** The code manually maps diffState to EdgeDiffState:
  const edgeDiffState: EdgeDiffState = resourceDiff === "added" ? "added" : resourceDiff === "removed" ? "removed" : "unchanged";

This is exactly what toEdgeDiffState(diffState) from graph-types.ts already does. The helper exists and is used in build-resource-graph.ts, but build-plan-graph.ts reimplements it inline.

**Fix:** Replace the 2-line ternary with toEdgeDiffState(resourceDiff). One-line change.

title: Harden input validation — crashes on malformed plan data
description:
## Problem

Four crash bugs in the Python package where malformed/unexpected input causes unhandled exceptions (raw tracebacks) instead of friendly DagshundError messages.

## Bug 1: `_render_resource` crashes on non-dict `changes`
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around line 113
- The code does `for field_name, change in sorted(changes.items())` assuming `changes` is a dict
- If `changes` is a string, list, int, or any non-dict truthy value AND the action is in `UPDATE_ACTIONS`, it crashes with `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'`
- The guard `if changes and action in UPDATE_ACTIONS` only checks truthiness, not type
- The `fixtures/invalid-plan.json` fixture has `"changes": "should_be_object"` — it only dodges the crash because its action is `"invalid_action_type"` (not in UPDATE_ACTIONS)
- **Fix**: Add an `isinstance(changes, dict)` check before iterating, or silently skip non-dict changes

## Bug 2: Individual change entries assumed to be dicts
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around line 114
- Inside the changes loop, `change.get("action", "")` assumes each change VALUE is a dict
- If a change value is a string, None, or integer → `AttributeError`
- **Fix**: Add `isinstance(change, dict)` guard or skip non-dict change values

## Bug 3: `render_text` crashes when `plan` value isn't a dict
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around lines 201-208
- If JSON has `"plan": "not_a_dict"` or `"plan": [...]`, the truthiness check passes
- Then `_all_unchanged(plan)` calls `plan.values()` → `AttributeError`
- Same for plan entries that are None or strings — downstream functions call `.get()` on them
- **Fix**: Validate `isinstance(plan, dict)` after extracting it, raise DagshundError if not

## Bug 4: `read_plan` doesn't catch `UnicodeDecodeError`
- **File**: `src/dagshund/cli.py`, around line 54
- `open(..., encoding="utf-8")` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on binary/corrupt files
- `UnicodeDecodeError` inherits from `ValueError`, NOT `OSError`
- Neither `except FileNotFoundError` nor `except OSError` catches it
- Users get a raw Python traceback instead of a friendly DagshundError
- **Fix**: Add `except UnicodeDecodeError` or `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError)` that wraps it in DagshundError

## Acceptance Criteria
- All four bugs produce a friendly DagshundError message instead of a raw traceback
- `just check` passes after fixes
- Do NOT add tests in this issue — tests are tracked separately in the test hardening issue
close_reason: All four crash bugs fixed with guards + 5 new tests, 99 passing, 100% coverage

title: Generalize serving endpoint lateral edge extractor to declarative spec
description: The serving endpoint → registered_model extractor traverses config.served_entities[] to extract entity_name from each element. This is one-to-many (one endpoint → multiple models). Consider extending LateralEdgeSpec to support array-valued field extraction (e.g. extractFields returning string[]) so the runner can map over elements. The nested JSON traversal is the bespoke part — a spec with an array-aware extractField could handle this.

title: Clean up SKILL.md and README after marketplace listing
Fix synthetic fixtures with empty remote_state.tasks
description:
Multiple synthetic fixtures have jobs with action 'update' but remote_state.tasks is an empty array. This causes all dependency edges to show as green (added) because the edge diff compares against empty remote dependencies.

Affected fixtures:
- all-hierarchies-plan.json: resources.jobs.etl_pipeline (3 tasks)
- complex-plan.json: resources.jobs.data_quality_pipeline (9 tasks)
- complex-plan.json: resources.jobs.etl_pipeline (5 tasks)

Fix: populate remote_state.tasks to match new_state tasks (matching a real update scenario). Use the unsanitized real fixtures as reference for realistic remote_state structure.

title: CLI: field paths with task prefixes and array indices are too long
description:
Field change lines in the CLI are too long and noisy, especially for for_each_task entries with repeated patterns. Example:

  ~ tasks[task_key='small_tables_RAW_3'].for_each_task.task.libraries[0].whl: "...whl" -> "...whl"

The field path alone is 66 chars before the value even starts. With dozens of for_each_task entries all showing the same library change, this is unreadable.

Options:
- Strip the tasks[task_key='...'] prefix and show the task key separately (or group by task)
- Collapse repeated identical changes across tasks into a summary (e.g. '12 tasks: libraries[0].whl changed')
- Shorten the path by abbreviating common prefixes (for_each_task.task -> fet)

title: consolidate thin context hooks into hooks/contexts.ts
description:
Five context+hook pairs exist as separate files, each a 6-30 LOC wrapper around createContext + useContext with zero behavior:

- hooks/use-plan-context.ts (7 LOC)
- hooks/use-lateral-isolation.ts (6 LOC)
- hooks/use-job-navigation.ts (6 LOC)
- hooks/use-interaction-context.ts (30 LOC — larger because the state type is wide, but still pure wiring)
- hooks/use-tab-visibility.ts (6 LOC)

Plus two type-only context declarations in the types/ folder that are the same pattern:
- types/phantom-context.ts (9 LOC)
- types/lateral-context.ts (14 LOC)

Action:
- Consolidate all five into hooks/contexts.ts (or hooks/context-reads.ts). One file with the context objects and read hooks grouped by domain.
- Fold types/phantom-context.ts and types/lateral-context.ts into the same file (or colocate with the providers that use them).
- Update imports across components and hooks.

Rationale:
- Discoverability: today a consumer can't tell from the import whether a hook is a thin context read or real logic. Grouping the thin ones signals 'just context wiring'.
- Adding a new context property becomes one edit, not a new file + hook + re-export.

Devil's advocate:
- 'Files are cheap; colocation with providers is clearer.' True if providers lived per-file, but the providers are mostly in app.tsx and flow-canvas.tsx, so colocation isn't the actual structure today.

Acceptance: 5 files → 1 file. No behavioral change. All imports updated.

title: Move diff-state-styles.ts from components/ to utils/
description: diff-state-styles.ts is a pure data module (no JSX, no React) that lives in components/. It is imported by graph/layout-graph.ts and hooks/use-node-dimming.ts, creating two upward layer violations. Fix: move to utils/diff-state-styles.ts and update import paths.

title: adopt PyPI attestations when GitLab has blessed path
description:
Track the ecosystem until a blessed, non-experimental path exists for producing PEP 740 attestations from GitLab CI, then adopt it in the release pipeline.

Context (as of 2026-04-10):
- Trusted publishing from GitLab CI works (we already use it via PYPI_ID_TOKEN / aud=pypi).
- Producing attestations is still GitHub-Actions-first. The pypi-attestations CLI README explicitly says it is 'intended primarily for experimentation', and the PyPI docs open the manual-generation section with 'STOP! You probably don't need this section'.
- Nov 2024 HN thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42136375): PyPI maintainer promised GitLab/other providers would get attestation support 'in short order'. 17 months later that still has not shipped.
- DIY is the wrong move per PyPI's own guidance. Do NOT hand-roll sigstore-python glue into build: just to get the attestation badge now.

What to watch for:
- pypi-attestations removing the 'experimentation' disclaimer.
- A first-class GitLab section in https://docs.pypi.org/attestations/producing-attestations/.
- uv publish gaining native attestation generation (not just upload).

When any of those ship: add a SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN id_tokens block to the build job, run the blessed attestation tool against dist/*.whl, and verify the attestation badge appears on the test.pypi.org release before cutting over to prod.

Referenced from a TODO in .gitlab-ci.yml next to the publish jobs.

title: Remove dead halfW math in chooseLateralHandles
description: In layout-graph.ts chooseLateralHandles, line 356 computes sourcePos.x + halfW - (targetPos.x + halfW) which simplifies to sourcePos.x - targetPos.x. The halfW cancels out and is dead math. Remove it for clarity.

title: CLI: diff output lines too long — field paths and values
description:
Two issues making CLI diff lines too long:

1. Values (already partially fixed): truncation to last 40 chars helps but combined old -> new is still ~90 chars before the field path even starts.

2. Field paths: paths like tasks[task_key='small_tables_RAW_3'].for_each_task.task.libraries[0].whl are 66+ chars alone. With dozens of for_each_task entries all showing the same library change, this is unreadable.

Options:
- Strip task prefix and group by task
- Collapse repeated identical changes across tasks into a summary
- Shorten common path prefixes
- Further reduce value truncation threshold

title: Inconsistent lateral isolation naming
description: isolatedLateralNodeId vs lateralIsolatedIds use inconsistent word ordering. Pick one convention (e.g. lateralIsolated* everywhere) and rename for consistency.

title: Replace magic exit codes with an IntEnum in cli.py
description:
src/dagshund/cli.py:250 has:

  sys.exit(3 if needs_attention else 2)

And the help text for -e/--detailed-exitcode (cli.py:95) says 'Exit 2 if safe changes, 3 if dangerous actions or drift, 0 if none (for CI)'. The numbers are also implied by other sys.exit() calls elsewhere (1 for DagshundError).

Replace with:

  class ExitCode(IntEnum):
      CLEAN = 0
      ERROR = 1
      SAFE_CHANGES = 2
      DANGEROUS = 3

Then help text references values via f-string so docs can't drift from the actual codes:

  help=f'Exit {ExitCode.SAFE_CHANGES} if safe changes, {ExitCode.DANGEROUS} if dangerous actions or drift, {ExitCode.CLEAN} if none (for CI)'

And sys.exit(ExitCode.DANGEROUS if needs_attention else ExitCode.SAFE_CHANGES).

Small win. Bundle with dagshund-161c (typed model) or another cli.py touch — not worth a dedicated MR on its own.

title: Add aria-live to search match count

title: fix: debounce node hover to prevent flickering on crowded graphs
description: On crowded graphs, moving the mouse quickly across nodes causes rapid highlight/dim toggling on every node, creating visual flicker. Add a short debounce (50-100ms) to the hover state in useNodeDimming so highlights only apply after the cursor settles on a node. Beads: dagshund-2ji

title: parseThreePartName fails on UC names containing dots
description: extract-resource-state.ts:70-78 splits on '.' and requires exactly 3 parts. Unity Catalog allows dots in backtick-quoted catalog/schema/table names. A name like my.catalog.schema.table would split into 4 parts and return undefined, making the resource an orphan in the graph. First step: investigate how databricks bundle plan -o json serializes backtick-quoted UC names to determine if this is reachable.

title: detect drift: warn when remote differs from old in changes
description: Changes can have old, new, AND remote fields. Usually remote === old, but they diverge when someone edited the resource outside the bundle (manual drift). We could detect remote != old and surface a warning in both text and browser output. Could be feature creep — the CLI already handles drift by using remote as the baseline. Evaluate whether the visual indicator adds value or just noise.
close_reason: Duplicate of dagshund-2umf which has more detail

title: Snapshot tests for terminal text output
description:
Golden-file smoke tests for the installed dagshund CLI. Tests the actual packaged binary (not source) against every fixture × flag combination.

## Scope

### Golden files in tests/golden/
Store expected CLI output for every combo:
- Each fixture (sample, complex, no-changes, all-hierarchies, mixed) plain
- Filter flags: -a, -r, -m, -c with relevant fixtures
- Search filter: -f 'type:jobs', -f 'status:added', -f 'pipeline', -f '"etl_pipeline"'
- Compositions: -c -f 'type:alerts', -a -r
- HTML output: just verify file is non-empty and contains <html (no golden file for HTML content)
- --version output

CI has no TTY so output is plain text — golden files generated the same way.

### CI smoke stage
Add a smoke stage between build and release in .gitlab-ci.yml:
- Runs on every push (builds wheel locally if no build artifact)
- On tags: tests the actual build artifact from the build job
- Installs wheel in isolated uv venv, runs dagshund against fixtures
- Diffs output against golden files — any drift fails the pipeline
- Gates the release: publish-test needs smoke to pass

### just recipes
- just update-golden — regenerate all golden files from current source
- just test-golden — run golden file comparisons locally

### Cleanup
- Remove the grep-based assertions from existing subprocess smoke tests in test_cli.py that are now redundant (the golden files are strictly better)

Catches: formatting drift, missing sections, broken summaries, warning text changes, packaging issues (missing template, broken entry point).

title: Extract buildPhantomNodesFromEntries helper to deduplicate phantom collector conversion
description: Three phantom collectors (collectPhantomDatabaseInstances, collectPhantomAppDependencies, collectPhantomWarehouseAndDashboardRefs) share identical PhantomEntry → PhantomGraphNode[] + edges conversion (~8 lines each). Extract a shared buildPhantomNodesFromEntries(phantoms: Map<string, PhantomEntry>, parentId: string) helper. This was explicitly flagged for follow-up by closed bead dagshund-l3uk when a third collector was added.

title: fix: add aria-pressed to filter toggle buttons
description: Filter toolbar buttons visually change on active state but don't communicate to assistive tech. Fix: add aria-pressed={isActive} to each filter button in diff-filter-toolbar.tsx.

title: Chain icon on nodes with lateral edges, click to isolate that node's links
description: Add a small chain/link icon in the bottom-right corner of any node that participates in lateral edges. When clicked, the view should isolate to show only the lateral edges from/to that specific node (dimming everything else). This gives a focused view of a single node's cross-resource relationships without the noise of all lateral edges at once. Different from the global Links toggle (which shows all lateral edges) — this is per-node isolation. The icon should only appear when the global Links toggle is active, or always be visible as an affordance. UX details TBD.

title: add cluster instance pool graph edges
description: Produce real direct-engine plans from a fixture workspace that supports instance pools, inspect instance_pool_id and driver_instance_pool_id for top-level clusters and applicable nested job cluster shapes, then decide and implement evidenced graph edges to instance_pools. Resolve bundle references and deployed API IDs only where observed. Add TypeScript and browser graph coverage. Postponed from dagshund-am23 because instance pools are unavailable in the current free fixture workspace.

CLI 1.14 bundle schema and bundle validation confirm symbolic .id references for top-level clusters, job_clusters[].new_cluster, tasks[].new_cluster, and pipeline clusters. Added lateral edges for those exact shapes, including worker and driver pool fields, remote-state fallback, deduplication, resource-graph coverage, and explicit rejection of .name references and concrete API IDs. Browser rendering confirmed by the user.

title: Fix correctness bugs: focusNodeId race and missing deleted run_job edges
description:
Two behavioral bugs found in TS review:

1. **focusNodeId effect fires before layout is ready** (flow-canvas.tsx:142-154): The useEffect for focusNodeId pans to a node without checking layoutState.status === 'ready'. If the layout is still loading, getInternalNode returns undefined, onFocusComplete() clears the request, and the pan never happens. Fix: guard on layout status.

2. **buildRunJobEdges skips deleted tasks** (build-plan-graph.ts:239-266): Deleted tasks with run_job_task references don't get cross-job edges, even though their nodes appear in the graph. Fix: include deleted tasks when scanning for run_job_task references.
close_reason: Both bugs fixed and verified in browser. focusNodeId race resolved with layout status guard + setTimeout. Deleted run_job edges now included.

title: evaluate tooling version bumps (Python + JS)
description:
Audit & bump dev/runtime tooling to current stable versions. Not a blind upgrade — evaluate each, decide, document reason if skipped.

## Python side (check pyproject.toml, prek.toml, justfile)
- uv (build + venv manager)
- pytest, pytest-cov
- ruff (lint + format)
- ty (typechecker) — this one moves fast and has known incompatibilities; pin carefully
- prek (pre-commit hook runner)
- Python itself — currently pinned to >=3.12; 3.13 is stable, 3.14 is out (CI runs on 3.14 per pytest log)

## JS side (check js/package.json, js/bun.lockb)
- Bun (currently 1.3.8 per MEMORY)
- TypeScript (tsc)
- Biome (lint + format)
- React 19.x — check for patch bumps
- Zod (currently 4.3.6 per MEMORY — note v4 lowercase error messages gotcha)
- React Flow (@xyflow/react)
- elkjs
- Tailwind CSS v4.x
- Vitest (JS test runner)

## Approach
1. List current versions: `uv pip list`, `cd js && bun pm ls`
2. For each, check latest stable + breaking-change notes
3. Propose bumps grouped by risk: patch/safe (bundle together), minor (one MR), major (separate MR each, with migration notes)
4. Update MEMORY version quirks if Zod/Bun/React versions change

Skip: ruff rule additions, biome rule migrations — those belong in separate beads so the bump stays mechanical.
close_reason: Audit complete. Six child beads filed (3ilg, 27t0, 3efn, 31gc, 3q4j, 9ztv) covering every proposed bump, grouped by risk as the bead description prescribed.

title: add Vector Search index endpoint graph edge
description: Produce a real direct-engine plan from a fixture workspace that supports Vector Search endpoints and indexes, inspect how endpoint_name is emitted in new_state and remote_state, then add an evidenced resource-graph relationship from vector_search_indexes to vector_search_endpoints. Resolve only identities supported by the observed plan and add TypeScript and browser graph coverage. Added lateral resolution for the exact symbolic .name reference and concrete endpoint names present in plan state, including remote-state and resource-graph coverage, while rejecting symbolic .id and endpoints absent from the plan. Browser rendering confirmed by the user.

All handle unknowns gracefully (wildcard/catch), but a new Databricks action type requires updating all three. description: R3-LOW-28. loadFixture function is duplicated in js/tests/graph/build-plan-graph.test.ts and build-resource-graph.test.ts with identical implementation: reads fixture file, parses with parsePlanJson, throws on failure. Fix: create js/tests/helpers/load-fixture.ts with the shared function and import from both test files. Flagged by: Code Quality (HIGH).

title: Refactor FlowCanvas state to useReducer
description:
Consolidate the 7 useState calls in flow-canvas.tsx into a single useReducer.

Current state: 7 independent useState calls (selectedNode, selectedNodeId, hoveredNodeId, filterDiffState, showLateralEdges, showPhantomLeaves, isolatedLateralNodeId) with coordinated multi-set patterns in handlePaneClick, handleClosePanel, and handleNodeClick.

What changes:
- Define CanvasState type and CanvasAction discriminated union
- Replace 7 useState with one useReducer
- selectedNode + selectedNodeId merge into one field (selectedNode carries id), eliminating the state duplication where DagNodeData omits the node id
- Scattered set* calls become named dispatches (CLEAR_SELECTION, SELECT_NODE, HOVER_NODE, SET_FILTER, TOGGLE_LATERAL_EDGES, TOGGLE_PHANTOM_LEAVES, ISOLATE_LATERAL)
- The ~15 useMemo derivations stay unchanged, just read from state.fieldName

What it doesn't change:
- File size stays roughly the same (reducer function adds ~30 lines, removes ~20 lines of useState/set*)
- useMemo derivation chain is untouched
- useCallback handlers still needed for referential stability, just become one-liner dispatches

Discovered during React Crusade audit (W3 state duplication + W4 useState count).

title: Lateral edges between synced tables and their source-table phantoms
description: Add lateral edges connecting synced_database_tables resources to their source-table phantom nodes. Currently synced tables and their source-table phantoms both appear in the UC tree but have no visual connection — they're linked only implicitly by sharing a schema parent. A lateral edge from the synced table resource node to its source-table:: phantom (derived from spec.source_table_full_name) would make the data lineage relationship explicit. These would be extracted in extractLateralEdges or a similar step, using the same source_table_full_name field that creates the phantom.

title: Lateral edge extraction: consistency and collision fixes
description:
Three related issues from review:

1. Missing nodeIds.has(sourceNodeId) guard in extractDatabaseInstanceEdges and extractServingEndpointModelEdges — inconsistent with extractWarehouseEdges which does the check. Low risk since nodeIdByResourceKey is built from allNodes, but should be consistent.

2. Lateral edge IDs use the same source→target format as hierarchy edges. If a lateral edge coincides with a depends_on or hierarchy edge, duplicate IDs would confuse React Flow. Prefix lateral IDs with 'lateral::' to guarantee uniqueness.

3. extractPipelineTargetEdges could emit duplicate edges for the same pipeline→schema pair if ingestion_definition.objects has redundant entries. Add a seen-set dedup within the function.

title: LateralDependencyEntry and PhantomContextEntry share fields
description: Both types share label, resourceKey, and resourceType fields. LateralDependencyEntry adds nodeId and diffState. Could extract a shared base type, but they serve different conceptual purposes so keeping separate is also defensible.

title: Clean up useNodeDimming exports and unused return fields
description: NodeDimmingResult type is exported but never imported outside use-node-dimming.ts. Several return fields (isDimmed, dimOpacity, isHovered, isSelected, isFilterHighlighted) are computed but never destructured by any caller. Unexport the type and consider removing or lazy-computing unused fields.

title: Surface drift between remote and old state in plan
description:
Detect when a job was manually edited outside the bundle (break glass) and warn in CLI output.

Detection rule: for each change entry, if old is defined AND new is defined AND old == new, but remote differs or is absent, that field was silently changed by the server. The most reliable signal is edit_mode flipping from UI_LOCKED to EDITABLE — this is a binary indicator that someone broke glass.

Scope: CLI text mode warning only. The browser visualization already shows the correct remote→new delta after the dagshund-j5zd fix. Adding drift hues to the graph creates combinatorial visual complexity (modified-with-drift? added-but-drifted?) and the edge coloring problem is unsolvable without a new color language. A CLI warning before the diff output is sufficient.

Example output:
  ⚠ drift detected: resources.jobs.drift_pipeline was manually edited
    edit_mode, tasks[task_key=publish].depends_on[0].task_key, tasks[task_key=transform]

Fixture: fixtures/drift-plan.json (captured from real Databricks deployment with manual edits).
close_reason: Implemented — CLI warns inline and in summary when resources were manually edited outside the bundle

title: Unify repository-owned preparation and working-tree verification
description:
Make prek.toml the authoritative definition of all repository checks: existing formatting/lint/type/hygiene/security/lock hooks plus the full JS and Python unit suites and golden checks. All checks run as normal commit hooks; no manual-only stage. Unit/golden hooks run without filename arguments and always run. just check and CI invoke native uv run prek run --all-files; retain existing focused commands, with focused test recipes delegating to the same hook definitions. Remove the superseded check.py and add no Python/Bash runner, custom enumeration, hook interpreter, or second check list.

Stage intended additions before validation so native all-files selection includes them. It also checks current on-disk edits to tracked files. Native fixes retain normal failure behavior: inspect changes, restage intended fixes, and rerun. The check command never stages, retries, restores, or commits. No commit merely to validate. Preserve native selection/exclusions, generated-file policy, dependencies, ordinary hooks and signing/auth.

Use native concise reporting and quiet test reporters. Document optional verbose output capture for complete local logs; CI retains job output and coverage artifacts. Keep unrelated security/release/compatibility gates unchanged.

User authorized direct rework on retained feat/agent-first-check, then explicitly requested MR !108 reopening and commit/push of the revised work. Preserve normal hooks/signing/auth; no main merge is authorized.

Agent-first public interface: expose only install, dev, build, check, regen, gen-expected, and test-py-supported. Hide focused test/lint/format/typecheck helpers and hooks-run while preserving their callability. Agents use just check as the routine validation gate, relying on native prek summaries and expanding successful output only for diagnosis. Normal commit hooks enforce the same suite; do not bypass them or add a custom runner/output-filtering layer.

Approved follow-up (comment 1436): normal native hooks rebuild browser assets before tests; missing generated templates fail rather than silently skip tests. Keep supported Python coverage complete, reuse quality template artifacts in compatibility CI jobs, and run existing distribution/installed-wheel smoke verification for MRs as well as tags without weakening mandatory tag/version gates. Keep source/generated-output maps navigation-only, mandate just check for every change, and keep transient workflow history in Beads rather than durable docs. Documentation follow-up: local repository examples and agent/maintenance instructions use direnv exec, with an explicit checkout cd when invoked from outside it. .envrc continues loading the declared Nix toolchain; do not nest an extra nix develop shell or auto-approve direnv. Keep development workflow guidance in AGENTS.md and focused guidelines, not a README Development section.

- [ ] A checkout without generated browser assets passes the full gate only after native template generation; missing assets otherwise produce an actionable test failure, not skipped browser tests. Python 3.12/3.13/3.14 run the complete suite.
- [ ] MR and tag lanes both build distributions and smoke-test the installed wheel; tag version validation remains mandatory. Compatibility jobs consume the generated quality template rather than silently skipping tests.

Durable docs retain contracts/provenance, not transient task progress. Shared case vectors and golden expectations remain unchanged.
- [ ] Active local command documentation uses direnv exec; no stale nix develop examples remain outside historical Beads evidence. README has no Development section. Verify just check through direnv alone, preserving existing environment declarations and auth/approval gates.

F2 (medium): command logging breaks the explicit byte-safe filename requirement before native hooks run. `find_working_tree_paths` correctly uses `os.fsdecode` (line 35), but `run_stage` encodes `shlex.join(command)` with strict UTF-8 at line 44. title: Implement: Adopt shared checks in CI and development guidance
description:
## Outcome and prerequisites
Adopt the authoritative working-tree procedure from dagshund-2v9c.1 in CI and development/agent instructions. Depends on that implementation's interface: `python fixtures/tooling/check.py`, which executes Python safe fixes, native prek against tracked plus non-ignored untracked paths, JS/Python coverage tests, and golden --check; logs live under `.cache/check/<unique-run>/`. Public local command is only `just check`, not new fix/prepare/verify aliases. Parent comment 1408 permits native mutation and requires reviewing the final diff/capturing review targets only after complete success.

## Change sites
- `.gitlab-ci.yml`: current quality extends `.release-setup`, has MR/tag/main rules, individually runs six commands, and uses coverage regex `/(?i)total.*? (100(?:\.0+)?\%|[1-9]?\d(?:\.\d+)?\%)$/`. `.release-setup` already supplies Python/uv, Bun, Git-capable base image, `uv sync --locked`, and frozen Bun install. CI has no just, so call the same Python script directly, without adding packages or a Nix bootstrap.
