title: Implement: Resolve App Autoscaling database bindings
description:
## Outcome and accepted capture
G3: resolve App resources[].postgres to Lakebase Autoscaling database identity. m1oo.8/.12/.13 are CLOSED and accepted. Baseline main 222beec031ed51a9385952609cd50357f80b0f02; dagshund-m1oo/comment1280 and fixtures/COVERAGE.md G3. fixtures/golden/agent-app/plan.json SHA256 3ff9e8c00ec1ef649e76f03f1c5af51b3bbae8f5d4f33952e149943ea1277fa3 contains resources.apps.retail_assistant binding session_database: branch=projects/retail-agent/branches/production; database=projects/retail-agent/branches/production/databases/agent-sessions; permission=CAN_CONNECT_AND_CREATE. Target resources.postgres_databases.agent_sessions already exists under resources.postgres_branches.production. The App -> database edge is absent. AI Search is the selected knowledge path: no pgvector/second knowledge database fixture is pending.

## Implementation
1. Reproduce with buildResourceGraphFromPlan from js/tests/helpers/build-graphs-from-plan.ts and bun run js/scripts/extract-graph.ts fixtures/golden/agent-app/plan.json. resource_graph.edges.entries contains actual edge endpoints.
2. Extend js/src/preparation/prepare-app.ts AppResourceRef, APP_VARIANTS and projectRef with readonly postgres branch/database strings. Do not project permission as identity or add edges for it. Existing app-resources Projection and safe diagnostic handling own missing/malformed recognized variants; unknown variants remain opaque. prepare-plan.ts already supplies the selected current snapshot.
3. Normalize the actual database resource path before using the existing resolver: resolvePostgresCatalogDatabaseReference in graph/resolve-postgres-references.ts currently expects a bare database name, NOT the captured full /databases/... path. Export/rename that concrete branch+database-name resolver for both catalog and App consumers without changing catalog semantics. Add a narrow strict database-path parser alongside graph/postgres-paths.ts (projects/P/branches/B/databases/D, nonempty components, exact six segments). Normalize to project/branch/database identity and require its branch to agree with the App branch. Do not pass the full database path as the bare name, producing a doubled hierarchy.
4. App branch may use existing bundle .id/.name references to postgres_branches; database may use .id/.name references to an existing postgres_databases entry. Resolve through identityCatalog postgresBranchIdentityByResourceKey, postgresDatabaseIdentityByResourceKey, postgresResourceKeyByIdentity and postgresDatabaseResourceKeyByBranchRef. For a managed symbolic database, validate the supplied branch against the target's prepared parent/branch or resolved branch identity; no unresolved symbols become phantom names. ## Implementation
1. Reproduce with buildResourceGraphFromPlan and bun run js/scripts/extract-graph.ts fixtures/golden/agent-app/plan.json. Read resource_graph.nodes.entries and edges.entries. The existing positive assertion in js/tests/graph/agent-app-fixture.test.ts currently expects the WRONG App -> source-table::...agent_knowledge_index edge; replace it with the intended managed edge and assert the duplicate phantom is absent, rather than retaining that assertion as a permanent oracle.
2. Keep prepare-app.ts's existing uc_securable TABLE variant. In graph/build-reference-identity-catalog.ts add managed vector-search-index name aliases from effective extractStateField(entry, 'name'), accepting qualified names via parseThreePartName. Use a distinct vector-index alias namespace, not sourceTable aliases that would affect unrelated source-table owners. nodeIdByResourceKey supplies the actual managed node; no new index nodes or graph kinds.
3. In graph/resolve-app-references.ts TABLE resolution, resolve a whole-string ${resources.vector_search_indexes.<key>.name} or .id with extractBundleResourceIdRef before the qualified-name parse. Require matching resource type and an existing materialized managed key; unresolved/wrong-type symbolic references produce no guessed table phantom. This preserves current derived/synced-table alias precedence and limits the new identity consumer to App TABLE bindings. Do not add an invented App index variant, broad alias promotion or backend collision policy.
4. Preserve graph/resolve-uc-table-references.ts and resolve-workspace-references.ts source/endpoint/embedding relations and direct-access non-lineage semantics. Use existing ReferenceResolution/materialization/lateral dedup path, not a special emitter.
5. Extend js/tests/graph/agent-app-fixture.test.ts with the exact managed edge, absent duplicate phantom, and retained independent source and endpoint links. Add focused cases in graph/resolve-references.test.ts and build-resource-graph.test.ts; use extract-lateral-edges.test.ts for duplicate endpoint pairs. Test effective concrete name, symbolic first-deploy identity as a synthetic semantic case (the actual capture uses a concrete name), ordinary unmatched TABLE phantom, existing derived/synced alias precedence, repeated App bindings, missing/malformed names and selected-state empty/new/remote/delete cases. No new preparation projection is needed unless existing tests expose a task-scoped validation defect.

title: detail panel: topology-drift elements appear twice (Re-added + Unchanged)
description:
## Reproduction

Fixture: `fixtures/golden/manual-drift/plan.json`. `just dev fixtures/golden/manual-drift/plan.json`, click `drift_pipeline` → `publish` task. Browser detail panel shows:

    Re-added on apply
    (Present in your bundle but missing from the remote — will be recreated on apply.)
    + depends_on[task_key='transform']
    +   task_key: transform

    Removed
    depends_on[task_key='ingest']  [delete]
    - task_key: ingest

    Unchanged
    depends_on
    - task_key: transform          ← transform shown AGAIN here

The `transform` element appears in both **Re-added on apply** and **Unchanged**. Same payload rendered twice.

## Root cause

`modified-body.tsx:50-85` `filterUnmodifiedState` strips changed paths from `resourceState`. It consumes `fieldChanges` — the output of `splitMeaningfulChanges` in `filter-changes.ts:34-53`, which has already partitioned topology-drift entries into a separate `driftChanges` bucket.

So when `filterUnmodifiedState` walks `depends_on` to strip changed elements, it only knows about:

    tasks[task_key='publish'].depends_on[task_key='ingest']  (in fieldChanges)

and not about:

    tasks[task_key='publish'].depends_on[task_key='transform']  (in driftChanges — topology)

It strips `ingest` from the list, leaves `transform` intact, and the Unchanged section displays the remnant. Meanwhile, the topology-drift renderer (the "Re-added on apply" section) displays `transform` from its own path.

## Pre-existing

This is **not** introduced by dagshund-1naj. Pre-fix, the `ingest` entry was misclassified as `(remote)` and rendered under Modified, which muddied the same panel and made the Unchanged remnant less visually salient. The new clean section layout makes the duplication obvious.

## Fix direction

Option A — **pass topology-drift paths to the state filter too** (minimal change):
- Thread `driftChanges` into `ModifiedBody` (or derive from the same source).
- `filterUnmodifiedState` takes a combined path set (field + drift) when stripping.
- The Unchanged section then reflects what actually stays the same on apply.

Option B — **redefine Unchanged semantics**: "Unchanged" could either mean "fields the bundle declares" (current) or "fields that stay unchanged on apply" (what the user expects). Current behavior is the former. Option A implements the latter.

Recommendation: Option A. The section label is "Unchanged" which the user reads as "no change on apply" — that's the more useful semantics and lines up with how the Re-added section describes itself ("will be recreated on apply").

## Scope

- `js/src/components/detail-panel/modified-body.tsx` — `filterUnmodifiedState` takes a combined path set.
- Caller at `detail-panel` whichever assembles `fieldChanges` and `driftChanges` — thread the drift paths through.
- `js/tests/components/detail-panel/modified-body.test.tsx` — add a test: resource with topology drift on `depends_on[task_key='X']` should NOT show that element in the Unchanged section.

## Out of scope

- Python terminal/markdown — output is flat, there is no "Unchanged" section to dedupe against. The re-added section (`(re-added)` lines) coexists with the resource state only in the browser.

## Devil's advocate

*Maybe "Unchanged" should literally mean what the bundle has.* Then the duplication is correct. But the user is looking at a per-element breakdown and seeing the same element labeled both "will be recreated" and "unchanged" at once — that's self-contradictory. The label or the filter has to give.

*This might affect other topology-drift fixtures.* Yes — verify on `fixtures/golden/manual-drift/` after fixing. The `transform` task node itself (whole task) would also be in the task-list of the job's bundle state; does it duplicate too? Needs visual check.

## Related

Discovered during detail-panel review of dagshund-1naj fix. Same panel, different pre-existing defect.

title: Resource graph: support all DABs resource types consistently
description:
## Problem

The resource graph hardcodes UC resource types in multiple places:
- `UC_TYPES` set (catalogs, schemas, volumes, registered_models) — anything not listed falls to workspace
- Hierarchy edge logic checks `resourceType === "catalogs"` and `resourceType === "schemas"` literally
- Phantom catalog detection filters on `extractResourceType(key) === "catalogs"` only
- Jobs are excluded entirely from the resource graph (`isJobEntry` filter)

This means new UC types like `database_catalogs` silently render in the wrong bucket, and jobs don't appear at all.

## Full resource type mapping (from Databricks docs)

Ref: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/bundles/resources#supported-resources

### Unity Catalog hierarchy (catalog → schema → leaf)
- `catalogs` — top-level UC container
- `database_catalogs` — UC catalog backed by a Lakebase database_instance (same tier as catalogs)
- `schemas` — nest under catalogs
- `volumes`, `registered_models`, `synced_database_tables` — nest under schemas

### Workspace (flat)
- `jobs` — currently excluded from resource graph, should show as single nodes
- `pipelines`, `clusters`, `apps`, `dashboards`, `alerts`, `experiments`
- `model_serving_endpoints`, `sql_warehouses`, `secret_scopes`
- `database_instances` — Lakebase compute/storage, workspace-level
- `postgres_projects`, `postgres_endpoints`, `postgres_branches` — workspace-level
- `quality_monitors` — references UC tables but lives at workspace level

### Cross-graph edges
- `database_catalogs` references `database_instance_name` (workspace) — potential cross-graph edge

## What needs to change

1. **UC_TYPES**: add `database_catalogs` and `synced_database_tables`
2. **Catalog-tier detection**: treat both `catalogs` and `database_catalogs` as catalog-tier nodes (group nodes, phantom detection, hierarchy edges)
3. **Schema-tier detection**: already works for `schemas`, no change needed
4. **Leaf-tier detection**: `synced_database_tables` should behave like volumes (nest under schema)
5. **Jobs in resource graph**: remove the `isJobEntry` filter, render jobs as single nodes in the workspace bucket
6. **Make it consistent**: the categorization and hierarchy logic should be driven by data (sets/maps), not scattered string literals

## Scope
All changes in `src/graph/build-resource-graph.ts` and tests. The rendering components already handle external/phantom nodes generically.

title: split build-resource-graph.ts: extract hierarchy-chains.ts and build-nodes.ts
description:
graph/build-resource-graph.ts is 812 LOC and holds three separable concerns:

1. Node builders (lines 1-180): functions that convert plan entries into GraphNode objects.
2. Hierarchy chain specs (lines 182-345): TierSpec type + UC_CHAIN (line 225) + POSTGRES_CHAIN (line 286). These are two parallel blueprints for the same walker — structurally identical shape, ~60 lines each.
3. The chain walker itself (lines 345+): buildChainGraph and buildResourceGraph orchestration.

Action:
- Extract graph/hierarchy-chains.ts: TierSpec, ChainSpec, UC_CHAIN, POSTGRES_CHAIN, and any helpers used only by the chain specs.
- Extract graph/build-nodes.ts: the node builder functions that are pure entry → node converters.
- Leave the walker (buildChainGraph + buildResourceGraph + phantom injection glue) in build-resource-graph.ts.

Why now (not just size):
- Adding a third hierarchy (Unity Volumes, Clean Rooms shares, etc.) means copy-pasting a third ~60-line chain spec next to the other two. Having them in their own file makes the registry pattern obvious.
- The walker logic is the interesting part; co-locating it with 200 LOC of tier config hides it.

Devil's advocate:
- The first pass of the review argued the 812 LOC is cohesive. It is at the 'one algorithm' level, but not at the 'one reason to change' level — tier configs change independently from walker logic.

Acceptance: build-resource-graph.ts drops to ~400 LOC; hierarchy-chains.ts holds TierSpec + the two chains; build-nodes.ts holds pure node builders. No behavioral change; all tests pass.

comments.author: 6337146-chinchy@users.noreply.gitlab.com
comments.text:
Closing won't-fix. Already evaluated and stopped at this boundary in dagshund-1as7 (2026-03-14). Phantom collectors extracted there (800 -> 659 LOC); remaining structure deemed cohesive. Re-review:

- File grew 659 -> 812 LOC via feature additions (external leaf phantom refs, drift tracking, Postgres chain), not structural complexity. Same shape, more features.
- build-nodes.ts extraction: buildResourceNode / buildContainerResourceNode / buildRootNode / buildPhantomNode are called from 4+ internal sites (resolveEntryNode, resolveParentChain, buildWorkspaceGraph, buildChainGraph external-leaf injection). Relocating them turns section-local access into imports without DRY gain -- they are already single-definition.
- hierarchy-chains.ts extraction: TierSpec / ChainSpec types are co-defined with buildChainGraph semantics and have no other consumer. Splitting the type from its only walker fragments the contract; the files would evolve in lockstep anyway. UC_CHAIN + POSTGRES_CHAIN are ~90 LOC of data blobs tightly coupled to those types.
- "Third hierarchy coming (Unity Volumes, Clean Rooms)" is speculative -- no open bead proposes it. YAGNI; revisit if/when a 3rd chain actually lands.
- fake-dry-god-wrappers feedback applies in spirit: count actual shared lines vs. divergent logic before unifying. Here there is nothing to share -- pure relocation. Section markers already provide the navigability a split would.

Trigger to revisit: a 3rd hierarchy chain lands, or chain specs need plugin-style registration.

title: bump: bun 1.3.8 -> 1.3.12 (CI + @types/bun)
description:
Single MR owning all bun version churn in the repo.

## What to change

### .gitlab-ci.yml (lines 25-27) — CI runtime pin
Three values updated together:
- BUN_VERSION: "1.3.8" -> "1.3.12"
- BUN_SHA256: sha256 of bun-linux-x64.zip
- BUN_BIN_SHA256: sha256 of the extracted bun binary

1. curl -fsSL -o /tmp/bun.zip https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.12/bun-linux-x64.zip
2. sha256sum /tmp/bun.zip            # -> BUN_SHA256

4. sha256sum /tmp/bun-linux-x64/bun  # -> BUN_BIN_SHA256

title: Move stripTaskPrefix from change-entry.tsx to utils/task-key.ts
Implement: Correct state-only and gone cleanup semantics
description:
## Outcome and authority
Implement the cleanup half of epic dagshund-4fb0 after approval of the combined plan. This brief supersedes the old request for separate per-issue planning; it is a draft implementation contract, not execution authority. Preserve this ID and existing notes/evidence. Migrated from dagshund-n8zt.7; moving/closing that old record did not fix the bug. Parent comment 762 authorizes planning only. No prerequisite implementation bead.

## Binding presentation policy proposed for combined approval
A cleanup is action == delete AND (gone is literal true OR state_only is literal true). Missing, false or malformed flags do not suppress a real deletion; flags on other actions do not change semantics. Preserve the original action and flags, rather than rewriting delete to update. gone takes precedence for explanation: 'already absent; removing stale bundle state'. Otherwise explain 'removing from bundle state; backend resource is preserved'. Label the operation 'state cleanup', with '~' and normal modified/amber styling, never delete/red styling. Count it separately as 'state cleanup' in terminal/Markdown resource and run summaries. It is a safe change: detailed exit 2, ordinary exit 0. Existing real loss risks and actual drift anywhere in a mixed plan still yield exit 3 independent of display filtering. Cleanup itself does not predict future data loss or drift overwrite.

Use the EXISTING modified diff category for cleanup, with a visible 'State cleanup' badge/explanation on resource/job nodes and details. No new DiffState, filter toggle or CLI flag. --changes-only, --modified and status:modified include cleanup; --removed/status:removed exclude it. Browser Modified counts include cleanup nodes and Removed counts exclude them. Counts remain graph-node counts, not a new global operation-count system. Keep raw JSON disclosure historical and unchanged. Do not use the removed ObjectStateCard for cleanup or print 'No changes' in a cleanup detail panel.

Job-run cleanup is an effect, not a modification to its parent job. Keep the current parent diff/action and effect visibility/filter behavior; its detail is visible through the parent, not a newly invented effect filter. With state_only:true say 'run entry removed from bundle state; run history preserved'; gone uses the already-absent explanation instead of claiming a historical run exists. No play badge, no fires-on-deploy, no backend delete count. Preserve the existing unflagged legacy run-removal wording and semantics. dagshund-kftp will extend trigger presentation on top of this interface.

## Implementation route
1. At src/dagshund/model.py ResourceChange/parse_resource_change and JobRunEffect, retain cleanup flags and pass them in merge.py build_job_run_effect. Only literal true activates them (Python must not accept 1 as True). Preserve borrowed payloads and Plan.raw. In js/src/types/plan-schema.ts explicitly retain flags without rejecting previously accepted malformed opaque values; strict equality at the semantic boundary is sufficient. Carry them through utils/normalize-plan.ts buildJobRunEffect, orphan groups and standalone entries. Unknown fields and redaction behavior must remain supported.
2. Add small entry-aware cleanup and display-diff helpers in the existing Python plan.py and JS parser/map-diff-state.ts (keep action-only helpers for actual field changes). Gate classify_resource_loss_risk and cleanup drift detection on the cleanup predicate. detect_changes must continue treating cleanup as a change. Use the entry-aware path in Python filter.py/format.py and browser node/edge construction. Do not globally relabel delete actions or weaken DANGEROUS_ACTIONS.
3. title: Collapse large collections in transition diffs (list[object] readability)
description:
## Status (2026-04-14)

Shipped the minimal collapse-symmetry fix instead of the full element-wise diff (options A/B/C below).

### What changed

`format_display_value` now collapses dict/list values whose inline form exceeds `_INLINE_LIMIT` (60 chars) to `{N fields}` / `[N items]`, matching the behavior that `format_single_value` has always had for add-only/delete-only cases. `format_transition` routes through `format_display_value`, so transition diffs inherit the collapse for free.

Result for app-dependencies/expected.txt:

```
~ resources: [3 items] -> [6 items]
```

Instead of the previous two-line full-array dump.

### Why not full element-wise diff

Terminals can't show full structural diffs — it's just too much data for the CLI. The project convention everywhere else is "inline when small, summary when large". Doing element-wise `+ item / - item / ~ item` for list[object] diffs would be inconsistent with how every other collapsed value is rendered, and would drop huge walls of text into the terminal on large resource updates. The browser/DAG view is the right place for element-level structure — each app→resource ref is already an independent lateral edge there.

### Asymmetric collapse (kept)

Sides of a transition are collapsed independently:
- `[{task_key: "check_nulls"}] -> [3 items]` — left stays inline (short), right collapses (long)

This is an advantage: the shorter side often shows enough context to infer what changed (e.g. "had one task, now has three of something").

### Affected golden fixtures (regenerated)

- app-dependencies (resources array)
- task-dag-rewiring (depends_on)
- mixed-changes (depends_on)

### Out of scope (not implemented — see "why not" above)

- Element-wise `+ / - / ~` per list element
- Identity-key inference (name / task_key / key / id)
- Set-diff for lists of scalars
- Fallback paths for missing or duplicate identity keys

title: suppress wheel-version churn in text and browser output
description:
CI-built wheels bump versions on every run, so every task carrying libraries[N].whl shows as modified — drowning real changes in large DAGs.

Design (user-approved 2026-07-02):
- Wheel update := change key tasks[task_key='X'].libraries[N].whl, old/new parse as wheel filenames with the SAME distribution name (PEP 427 first segment). Different dist = real change. Scope is libraries[*].whl only (cluster tasks); serverless environments already surface wheels once per job.
- Text/md CLI: --suppress-wheel-updates flag. Drops wheel-update field lines (also on tasks that have other real changes — wheel info lives in one place), job still shows as update, and each job block ends with a wheel summary line per distinct wheel: 'wheel <dist>: <old> -> <new> (N tasks)'. Multiple distinct wheels per job supported.
- Browser: toolbar toggle. When on, tasks whose ONLY changes are wheel updates render as unchanged (dimming/filter counts follow); job container header shows the distinct wheel updates once. Detail panel stays unfiltered (drill-down truth). No relayout — both states computed at graph build time.
- Shared semantics mirrored Python/TS via shared test-vector fixture (like list-element-semantic-cases.json).
- New golden fixture with two wheel artifacts + version bumps + one real non-wheel change (needs workspace regen, user-run).

title: Show task-level changes summary on job group nodes
description:
When clicking a job group node (e.g. resources.jobs.data_quality_pipeline) that shows as 'modified', the detail panel currently only shows job-level changes (like depends_on updates) and unchanged job config fields. It does NOT show what changed inside the job at the task level.

For a modified job, the user wants to see a summary of task-level changes directly on the job node's detail panel:
- Added tasks: e.g. "+ check_duplicates, + check_references, + anomaly_detection" (green)
- Removed tasks: e.g. "- old_validation_task" (red)
- Modified tasks: e.g. "~ compute_statistics (depends_on changed)" (amber)

This gives a birds-eye view of what happened inside the job without clicking individual task nodes.

Similarly for added jobs: show all the tasks that were created as part of the job.
For removed jobs: show all the tasks that were deleted.

Implementation considerations:
- Job group nodes already have access to all their child task nodes in the graph
- Need to collect task-level diff states from child nodes and summarize them
- Could be a new section in the detail panel between job-level changes and unchanged config
- The task names should probably be clickable to navigate to that task node

Key files:
- src/components/detail-panel.tsx (add task summary section)
- src/graph/build-plan-graph.ts (job nodes may need references to child task diff states)
- src/types/graph-types.ts (DagNodeData may need child task summary info)

title: Derive phantom branch project from resource path
description:
Phantom branches (branches referenced by endpoints but not in the plan) currently attach directly to the Lakebase root because deriveParentRef is undefined — the branch identity alone (e.g. 'archive') doesn't encode which project it belongs to.

Now that parent fields use resource paths (e.g. projects/warehouse-replica/branches/archive), we have enough information to derive the project. The endpoint's parent path contains both project_id and branch_id.

Approach: make branch identities composite ({project_id}/{branch_id}) so deriveParentRef can split on '/' to extract the project_id. This requires:
- Branch resolveIdentity: extract project from parent field + branch_id → 'warehouse-replica/archive'
- Endpoint resolveParentRef: return composite identity matching branch format
- Branch deriveParentRef: identity.split('/')[0] → project_id
- Update phantom label extraction (currently splits on '.', needs to handle '/' separator)
- Update buildHierarchyId for composite identity
close_reason: Composite branch identities implemented, phantom branches now attach to their project

title: Replace vendored dagre.js with proper dependency
description:
The vendored src/vendor/dagre.js (2200 lines of CJS-to-ESM shim) is a hack to work around @dagrejs/dagre v2's ESM dist using dynamic require() that Bun's browser bundler can't trace. Investigate and test alternatives in order of least invasive:

1. **Direct import test** — try importing @dagrejs/dagre directly (no vendor) to see if Bun 1.3.8 handles it now
2. **esbuild prebundle as build step** — `bunx esbuild node_modules/@dagrejs/dagre/dist/dagre.cjs.js --bundle --format=esm --platform=browser --outfile=src/vendor/dagre.js` as a reproducible build:vendor script instead of a committed 2200-line file
3. **esm.sh CDN import** — `import dagre from 'https://esm.sh/@dagrejs/dagre'` to bypass bundler entirely (downside: requires internet)
4. **Switch to elkjs** — proper ESM, recommended by React Flow, more capable. Async API (returns Promise). ~30 line migration.

Test each option against `bun build` and `bun run dev`. Pick the least invasive one that works. If none of 1-3 work cleanly, go with elkjs.
close_reason: Superseded: switching to elkjs instead of fixing dagre vendor shim

title: fix: add loading indicator to FlowCanvas during ELK layout computation
description: R3-HIGH-6. After the plan loads, FlowCanvas shows an empty canvas with zero-count filter badges while ELK computes layout. GraphLayoutState starts as {status:'loading'} but FlowCanvas only handles the 'error' case — when loading, nodes/edges default to EMPTY_NODES/EMPTY_EDGES so React Flow renders blank. Fix: when layoutState.status === 'loading', render a centered 'Computing layout...' message with a pulse animation instead of the empty ReactFlow canvas. The existing LoadingIndicator in App.tsx only covers the stdin fetch phase, not the layout phase. Flagged by: UX (HIGH).

title: fix: remove .yaml/.yml from ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS in cli.ts or add clear error
description: R3-LOW-26. ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS in cli.ts:33 includes .yaml and .yml but parsePlanFromString only handles JSON via JSON.parse. A YAML file would fail with 'Invalid JSON' rather than 'YAML not supported'. Fix: either remove .yaml/.yml from the set, or detect YAML extensions and print a clear error: 'dagshund: YAML input not supported, convert to JSON first'. Flagged by: Code Quality (LOW).

title: expand test coverage: hooks + components (with happy-dom + testing-library)
description:
Current coverage is lopsided: graph/ 11/11, parser/ 2/2, utils/ 20/23 — but hooks/ 2/18 and components/ 0/~38. The React layer has no regression net, which makes refactors risky.

## Setup (one-time)

Add two devDependencies to js/package.json:
- @happy-dom/global-registrator (~3 MB) — DOM globals inside Bun test process
- @testing-library/react — component render + query helpers
- @testing-library/user-event (optional) — realistic interaction simulation

Wire happy-dom via bunfig.toml:
    [test]
    preload = "./tests/setup.ts"

Create js/tests/setup.ts:
    import { GlobalRegistrator } from '@happy-dom/global-registrator';
    GlobalRegistrator.register();

Zero runtime footprint — devDeps only, preloaded by bun:test.

## Phase 1 — hooks (pure, no new deps required)

Use the existing 18-LOC renderHook helper at tests/helpers/render-hook.ts. These hooks are pure computation + context reads:

- use-node-dimming (82 LOC — five orthogonal dim states; highest value)
- use-lateral-edge-state (50 LOC)
- use-styled-edges (47 LOC)
- use-value-format
- use-plan-context
- use-tab-visibility
- use-job-navigation
- use-lateral-isolation

## Phase 2 — hooks (effect-heavy, requires happy-dom)

After setup is in place:

- use-resize-handle (pointer events + refs)
- use-viewport-positioning (116 LOC, refs + effects)
- use-async-layout (async state + cancellation)
- use-stdin-plan (async I/O — may need fetch mocking)
- use-theme (localStorage + effects)

## Phase 3 — components (requires @testing-library/react)

Render with mock props, assert on DOM output. Prioritize by refactor risk:

- resource-node, task-node, hierarchy-node — TEST FIRST. These are about to be refactored under dagshund-2zyd (NodeFrame extraction); tests are the regression net.
- detail-panel subcomponents: action-badge, diff-state-badge, drift-pill, copy-button, change-entry, object-state-card, resource-state-view
- Interactive: search-bar, diff-filter-toolbar, lateral-edge-toggle, phantom-leaf-toggle, theme-toggle

## Out of scope (explicitly)

- flow-canvas.tsx — testing React Flow wiring requires mocking measurements; happy-dom does not do layout. Extract the dense useMemo block at flow-canvas.tsx:186-249 into its own hook in a separate bead and test the hook instead.
- ELK layout — runs in a Web Worker; not worth simulating.
- app.tsx / frontend.tsx / cli.ts — entry-point wiring; smoke coverage via existing html-assembler test is enough.

## Acceptance

- bunfig.toml preloads setup.ts; existing tests still pass.
- All 13 Phase 1+2 hooks have tests with at least one happy-path case and one edge case each.
- The three node components have tests before dagshund-2zyd lands.
- just test-js is green; coverage goes from ~35% to ~80% in the React layer.
- No production code modified to accommodate tests (per CLAUDE.md).

title: Add a complex multi-job fixture for testing
notes:
Current test fixture is a single job with a handful of tasks. A richer fixture would help stress-test layout, hover dimming, and the detail panel.

## Structure

**Job 1: ETL_PIPELINE (existing job, mostly unchanged)**
- Keep current tasks as-is
- Add a new task that triggers Job 2 via run_job_task referencing ${resources.jobs.DATA_QUALITY_PIPELINE} (DAB cross-job linking syntax)
- This trigger task should be 'added' diff state (new resource)

**Job 2: DATA_QUALITY_PIPELINE (new complex job)**
- 8-10 tasks with realistic Databricks names (validate_schema, check_nulls, compute_statistics, etc.)
- Deep dependency chain (4+ levels) to test ELK layout spacing
- Fan-in pattern: multiple validation tasks feed into a single aggregation task
- Fan-out pattern: one setup task spawns several parallel checks
- Mix of diff states: some added, some modified, one removed, rest unchanged
- Tasks with large change payloads (long field lists) to exercise detail panel scrolling
- Realistic notebook_task / python_wheel_task / run_job_task types

## Goal
Test cross-job edges, complex layout, and all visual states in a single fixture.

title: Golden fixtures: fill coverage gaps for lateral edges, phantoms, and cross-job vars
description:
All fixtures generated from scratch using the regeneration tooling (dagshund-2z0m). Existing fixtures like all-hierarchies-plan.json serve as reference for the kind of coverage we want, but nothing carries forward — everything is regenerated from real bundle configs via deploy/plan/capture/destroy.

## Golden output generation (owned by this bead)

After each plan.json is captured, run dagshund against it to produce expected terminal and markdown output:
- `dagshund < plan.json > expected.txt`
- `dagshund --format markdown < plan.json > expected.md`

These are committed alongside the plan.json in each fixture folder. CI tests (dagshund-39ue) diff against these files.

## Cleanup (owned by this bead)

When the golden suite is complete, delete all old fixtures and golden outputs:
- `fixtures/*.json` (old fixture plans)
- `fixtures/bases/` (old bundle configs)
- `tests/golden/*.txt` and `tests/golden/*.md` (old expected outputs)

The golden suite in `fixtures/golden/<name>/` replaces everything.

## Tier 1: Free Edition (generate locally)

### Diff state coverage
1. **all-create** — Fresh deploy, everything new. Jobs, schemas, volumes, experiments, registered_models.
2. **all-destroy** — Tear down everything. Same resources, all deleted.
3. **mixed-changes** — Adds + removes + updates + unchanged in one plan. Jobs with task changes, schema property edits, volume add/remove.
4. **no-changes** — Plan with zero diff. Everything skip/no_change.
5. **drift** — Remote state diverged from local config. Jobs or schemas modified out-of-band.

### Task dependency patterns
6. **task-dag-rewiring** — Tasks added/removed mid-DAG, edges change shape between before/after. Covers: linear chain, fan-out (1→N), fan-in (N→1), diamond (fan-out then fan-in).
7. **cross-job-interpolation** — run_job_task with ${resources.jobs.X.id} — job invoking another job.
8. **cross-job-new-target** — run_job_task where target job is newly created (id=0, vars-based resolution).

### Sub-resources
9. **permissions-lifecycle** — Permissions added, changed, removed on a parent that itself may or may not change.
10. **grants-lifecycle** — Grants added/changed/removed on schemas.

### Lateral dependencies (dagshund inventions, free-tier resources)
11. **alert-to-warehouse** — alert → sql_warehouse via warehouse_id. Phantom sql_warehouse if warehouse not in plan.
12. **app-dependencies** — app → jobs, warehouses, secret_scopes, endpoints, experiments. Phantom job, phantom secret_scope, phantom experiment, phantom warehouse, phantom endpoint.

### Hierarchy phantoms
13. **phantom-catalog-chain** — Volume/schema references catalog not in plan → phantom catalog. Tests UC hierarchy phantom generation.

## Tier 2: Enterprise Only (requires access to enterprise)

14. **pipeline-to-catalog** — pipeline → catalog/schema lateral edge, phantom catalog/schema. Requires Lakeflow pipelines.
15. **serving-endpoint-to-model** — model_serving_endpoint → registered_model lateral edge, phantom endpoint. Requires GPU/provisioned endpoints.
16. **lakebase-hierarchy** — synced_database_table → database_instance, source_table phantoms, postgres project/branch/endpoint hierarchy. Lakebase is enterprise-only. Reference: current all-hierarchies-plan.json shows this kind of coverage.
17. **external-locations** — External locations, advanced UC features. Enterprise UC features.

## Coverage crosscheck

| Dagshund concept | Fixture(s) |
|---|---|
| Diff states: create, delete, update, skip, drift | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 |
| Task deps: linear, fan-out, fan-in, diamond | 6 |
| Cross-job: interpolation, new target | 7, 8 |
| Sub-resources: permissions, grants | 9, 10 |
| Lateral: alert→warehouse | 11 |
| Lateral: app→everything | 12 |
| Lateral: pipeline→catalog/schema | 14 (enterprise) |
| Lateral: endpoint→model | 15 (enterprise) |
| Lateral: synced_table→db_instance | 16 (enterprise) |
| Lateral: synced_table→source_table | 16 (enterprise) |
| Phantom: catalog, schema | 13 |
| Phantom: job, warehouse, secret_scope, experiment, endpoint | 11, 12 |
| Phantom: source_table, database_instance | 16 (enterprise) |
| Phantom: postgres project/branch | 16 (enterprise) |

Free edition limitations: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/getting-started/free-edition-limitations
Free tier supports jobs (5 concurrent tasks), schemas, volumes, registered_models, experiments, alerts, apps (1), pipelines (1 active), model_serving_endpoints (limited, no GPU), sql_warehouses (1, 2X-Small).
Enterprise-only: Lakebase (database_instances, synced_database_tables, postgres hierarchy), external_locations, advanced UC.

17 total fixtures: 13 free-tier + 4 enterprise.

title: Stack job dependency blocks vertically with aligned left edges
description:
Large job DAGs have confusing placement between jobs even when task layout inside each job and dependency direction are correct. In the synthetic 11-job example from dagshund-8pte, large independent jobs stack vertically while the small orchestrator/worker group appears incidentally beside the upper/right end of that stack. Proximity makes unrelated jobs look grouped and small connected regions easy to miss. Task layout inside each job stays unchanged. Two bounded additions address observed usability defects: visible containers for taskless jobs and predictable initial framing of the Jobs view.

Agreed structure: a vertical stack of dependency blocks anchored to one shared left edge. An independent job is a one-job block. Jobs connected by existing job-dependency relationships belong to one block, including branches and joins. Each block lays out internally left to right and may occupy the horizontal space it needs. Normalize every block's leftmost edge to the same X coordinate. Place the next block below the lowest point of the entire preceding block with a 60-graph-unit gap, as accepted on the stress preview. Never tuck unrelated jobs beside another block, wrap blocks into columns, prioritize changed jobs, or fill spare space with independent jobs.

Order blocks alphabetically by the visible name of the starting job. For multiple starting jobs, use the alphabetically first starting job as the sort key; stable IDs resolve equal names. Scope is valid, acyclic DAB plans under decision comment 904. Preserve existing unsupported-input handling rather than inventing cycle support, roots or dependency meaning; bring concrete valid-plan counterevidence back for discussion.

Taskless jobs must have a visible, usable minimum-sized container and title bar even when they have zero rendered task children. Do not fabricate task nodes or change deleted-task rendering to achieve this. This is a narrow exception to the original dimension-preservation rule for taskless jobs only. Keep task-bearing job dimensions and all job-local task geometry unchanged.

Initial Jobs viewport: compose the top-left bounds of the first alphabetical block in the upper-left area with generous breathing room, clear of overlay controls. Trial placement is approximately 38% across and 38% down the usable canvas, the upper-left golden-section intersection. This places the block corner there; it must NOT center the viewport on that corner, pin content to the edges, or fit the entire long stack into unreadability. Use a readable starting zoom and measured bounds. Treat the composition as a visual trial to confirm, not a new user-facing ratio control. Apply only on initial presentation of a plan; do not reapply it after pan/zoom, selection, resizing, filtering or tab changes. Preserve explicit focus/search/node navigation and manual Fit view, plus existing Resources-view behavior.

Evidence: dagshund-8pte.2 comment 898; screenshot /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund-review-evidence/dagshund-8pte/ordering-stress-user.png; generator /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund-review-evidence/dagshund-8pte/assess-ordering.ts and graph-input evidence ordering-assessment.jsonl beside it. These are synthetic observations, not a live-workspace compatibility claim. Current issue evidence and baseline/candidate attribution for taskless containers and initial framing are dagshund-by22.1 comments 923 and 925, with review findings F2/F3 in dagshund-by22.1.1 comments 924/926.

Approach: reversible prototype, matched browser comparisons on stress, mixed sizes, branches/joins, multiple starts and truly taskless jobs, then user confirmation before productionizing. The existing stack/gap preference remains recorded; the revised empty-container and initial-framing result needs a fresh visual check. Retain independent review, semantic/layout regression tests, typecheck/lint/build and real-browser verification. Preserve headers, interior panning, selection and hover. Report unavailable real large plans honestly.

Non-goals: task layout changes within jobs, compact packing/grid layouts, changed-first ordering, minimaps, manual rearrangement, permanent selectors or ratio settings, new navigation controls, resource-view redesign or dependencies. The bounded additions above supersede earlier blanket freezes on all job dimensions/initial viewport behavior, not the remaining preservation boundaries. Productionization remains behind the separate visual gate and execution authorization.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every independent job or connected dependency group forms a block in an alphabetical vertical stack with a shared left edge. A block grows rightward according to existing relationships; the next begins below its full height with the accepted 60-graph-unit gap.
- Sort by visible starting-job name; multiple starts use the alphabetically first, with stable-ID ties. Preserve relationships/direction and deterministic placement. Supported-input scope is valid acyclic DAB plans; preserve existing unsupported-input handling without new cycle features.
- Truly taskless jobs render a visible minimum-sized container/title bar, not an invisible zero-area node. Only their dimensions may change for this purpose; task-bearing dimensions, task-local geometry and deleted-task semantics stay unchanged.
- On initial Jobs presentation, place the first block's top-left bounds near the user-approved 38% across/down composition, clear of toolbar overlays at readable zoom. Do not center on its corner, pin to edges, or squeeze the entire long stack into view.
- Initial anchoring is one-time per plan presentation and does not reset subsequent user navigation. Preserve explicit search/focus/node navigation, manual Fit view, header/task interactions, panning, hover and Resources-view behavior.
- User visual walkthrough and explicit confirmation on representative browser previews are sufficient visual acceptance evidence, including corrected empty jobs and initial composition. Screenshots, matched screenshot archives and exact browser/viewport/zoom metadata are optional, not blocking prerequisites. Record available observations, target/input identities and missing metadata honestly; do not invent measurements or automated browser proof. This user-approved evidence policy supersedes stricter earlier description/child capture requirements.
- Independently review subsequent changes and pass regression tests, typecheck, lint, build and applicable browser checks covering block invariants, empty-job bounds, initial positioning and preservation of existing interactions. Visual walkthrough acceptance does not waive code defects or automated checks.
- No packing/grid, changed-first ordering, manual rearrangement, permanent selector/ratio setting, new navigation controls, resource redesign or dependencies without separate agreement.
notes:
User agreed to record the concrete vertical-block direction: independent jobs and connected dependency groups share a left edge, blocks grow rightward as needed, and subsequent blocks begin below the full previous block. Alphabetical ordering by starting-job name, alphabetically first starting job for multi-start groups, and stable-identifier tie-breaking were accepted. This supersedes the earlier open-ended layout exploration; visual iteration now focuses on validating this structure and tuning spacing. Approval is for updating the bead only, not execution.
User explicitly approved the stated planning scope and planner handoff: vertical alphabetical dependency blocks with a shared left edge and full-height separation; between-job placement only; preservation of existing task/graph/header/pan/selection/hover behavior; reversible-prototype visual approval before productionizing. Planner must identify rootless/cyclic-group semantics as an explicit question rather than silently choosing. title: Implement: reversible vertical dependency-block prototype
description:
Planning-only draft under dagshund-by22. Do not start until coordinator explicitly authorizes prototype execution. Outcome: a small reversible browser prototype of the agreed vertical block structure, with comparable baseline evidence, not a packing-algorithm competition or production rollout. Follow repository TypeScript, visualization and testing guidelines.

Scope and input: valid DAB plans with acyclic job dependencies (parent decision comment 904). A block is a weakly connected component of existing cross-job relationships, independent jobs are singleton blocks. Use all existing graph.edges regardless of diffState, including removed run-job relationships already rendered. A starting job has no incoming cross-job edge in its block. Sort blocks by the alphabetically first starting job's visible header name, tie by stable job ID; do not use diff status or size. Visible name is extractResourceName(job.resourceKey), matching JobNode and buildJobFields; it is not resourceState.name. Preserve direction and every original rendered edge.

Selected minimal technical approach: retain the current single ELK compound layout and translate whole connected components after it. This preserves existing within-component RIGHT placement, all job dimensions, and exact job-local task positions while removing incidental global placement between unrelated components. Do not add nested React Flow block containers or extra ELK passes. Entry point js/src/graph/layout-graph.ts::toReactFlowElements currently does groupNodesByJob -> buildElkCompoundGraph -> getElk().layout -> extractLayoutData -> assembleFlowNodes. Insert pure grouping/translation between extraction and assembly. Reuse extractTaskNodeParentId from js/src/utils/resource-key.ts to map task endpoints to owning job IDs, just as collectCrossJobEdges currently does. Reuse the existing ELK options and job/task builders unchanged. Resource layoutResourceGraph must not change.

Steps:
1. Save a reproducible baseline revision/view before edits. Reproduce the stress input using /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund-review-evidence/dagshund-8pte/assess-ordering.ts: lateral-deps plus eight copies of wheel-bump's wheel_pipeline current value named stress_01..08. Its imports point to an OLD worktree: adapt imports in a scratch copy to the authorized checkout, do not depend on that path or modify historical evidence. Inputs are fixtures/golden/lateral-deps/plan.json and fixtures/golden/wheel-bump/plan.json. Prior evidence is dagshund-8pte.2 comment 898 and ordering-stress-user.png beside the script.
2. Implement a pure, readonly block transform consumed only by this jobs-layout entry point (a small js/src/graph/job-dependency-blocks.ts module is appropriate). Find weak components of mapped cross-job edges over every job group; ignore intra-job edges only for grouping and deduplicate job pairs. Determine zero-incoming start jobs and compare name.localeCompare(otherName), then stable ID by code-unit comparison for ties. Reuse that comparator for choosing the first start. Existing buildElkCompoundGraph input order/ELK settings stay intact.
3. For each ordered component compute minX=min(job.x), minY=min(job.y), maxBottom=max(job.y+job.height). Translate ONLY top-level job coordinates by dx=-minX, dy=nextTop-minY; begin nextTop=0, then nextTop += maxBottom-minY+gap. Copy the positions map rather than mutate its input; dimensions and task positions remain unchanged. Start visual spacing trials at 60 graph units, the existing root node spacing; this is provisional, not approved spacing. Keep translation logic separate from async ELK so pure tests can exercise it.
4. Supported inputs have a start in every component. Do not add cycle detection, validation UI, cyclic layout rules, dropped jobs/edges or SDK support. If no start is available for a component, preserve the existing whole ELK layout unchanged rather than invent a rootless sorting key. This compatibility guard retains the previous renderer, not a promised cyclic layout. Bring concrete valid-DAB counterevidence back to the coordinator.
5. Compare baseline and candidate at the same viewport and zoom, with both overview and readable-detail views. Include synthetic stress, mixed tall/wide/tiny jobs, a branch followed by join, two starts merging (one alphabetically later downstream job must not determine the block key), isolated/no-task jobs, and fixtures/golden/task-dag-rewiring/plan.json. Keep any fabricated plans in scratch evidence, not golden fixture regeneration. Ask for a real large plan if available without requesting credentials or claiming synthetic inputs establish workspace compatibility.
6. Exercise job header detail opening, pan through job interiors, task selection, hover neighbors and zoom. Record the prototype target, input artifacts, screenshots/observations and proposed final gap for user confirmation; stop at the gate. Any temporary comparison mechanism must be easy to remove and must not become shipped UI.

Verification commands from repository root, wrapped in direnv exec /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund: just typecheck-js; bun run --cwd js biome check src/ tests/ (non-mutating); bun test --cwd js tests/graph/layout-graph.test.ts; just dev <plan-file> for browser evidence. Bun layout tests document that ELK Worker integration is not reliable inside the Bun test runner; actual layout comparison belongs in the browser. This prototype is independently reviewed for scope/preservation and evidence, but that review cannot replace the user gate.

Non-goals: within-job task layout/options, graph building/reference semantics, UI redesign, resource view, compact packing, changed-first order, minimap/navigation additions, manual rearrangement, permanent selectors or dependencies.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reversible candidate and unchanged baseline can be opened in real browsers; no permanent layout selector, ratio setting or new dependencies.
- Synthetic stress, mixed-size, branch/join and multi-start examples demonstrate the alphabetical shared-left-edge stack, full-height separation, accepted 60-graph-unit gap and existing left-to-right relationships.
- Truly taskless jobs have visible, usable minimum-sized containers and title bars. Verify zero actual graph task children; do not change deleted-task rendering or fabricate tasks. Existing task-bearing dimensions and every job-local task position remain unchanged.
- Initial Jobs presentation anchors the first block's bounds near the user-approved upper-left composition (roughly 38% across/down usable canvas), at readable zoom and clear of overlays. Do not center on its corner, pin to edges or fit the entire long stack into unreadability.
- Apply anchoring only at initial plan presentation; preserve later pan/zoom, selection, resize/filter/tab interactions, explicit focus/search/node navigation, manual Fit view and Resources behavior.
- Record input/target identities, observed human browser feedback, accepted gap and interaction results. Screenshots and exact browser/viewport/zoom metadata are optional: direct user walkthrough confirmation is sufficient visual evidence. State unavailable metadata/real-plan coverage honestly. This approved policy supersedes the original description's capture/measurement mandates; it does not waive code review, graph/example correctness or regression checks.
- Present the revised result for explicit visual approval through dagshund-by22.2 before productionizing; link the user's actual confirmations to the reviewed target, not an agent opinion.
- Approved exception to the original description: taskless-job minimum bounds and Jobs initial-positioning paths may change for the parent-approved F2/F3 additions. Other translation/task/graph/Resources preservation boundaries remain in force.

title: Implement: production vertical dependency-block placement and regressions
description:
Planning-only draft. Do not begin before explicit user approval on dagshund-by22.2 and coordinator productionization authorization. Outcome: productionize only the approved prototype from dagshund-by22.1 with focused automated coverage and no prototype-only controls. Gate evidence supplies the approved gap and exact candidate revision, not fresh architectural discovery. If prototype approval changes the selected approach or scope materially, return for plan revision before work.

Binding scope: valid DAB plans with acyclic cross-job relationships, per dagshund-by22 comment 904. Between-job placement only. Every independent job is one block; each weakly connected group using existing PlanGraph.edges is one block. Include existing removed relationships, do not recompute semantics from plan JSON or resource lateral edges. Sort blocks by alphabetically first zero-incoming starting job's visible header name; ties use stable job ID. Use extractResourceName(job.resourceKey) as JobNode does (buildJobFields currently sets label to the same value). Use localeCompare for names, existing project convention, and code-unit ID comparison for ties. No changed-first rule, packing, columns, manual rearrangement, navigation additions, permanent selector or new dependencies.

Exact change sites and path: js/src/hooks/use-plan-graph.ts calls buildPlanGraph and toReactFlowElements. js/src/graph/layout-graph.ts::toReactFlowElements groups jobs, builds the current compound input, awaits getElk().layout, extracts positions/dimensions and assembles React Flow nodes. Keep that single ELK invocation, buildElkCompoundGraph options, topologicalSortTasks and intra-job children/edges unchanged. Preserve task layout by translating entire dependency components AFTER extractLayoutData and BEFORE assembleFlowNodes. Reuse the prototype pure helpers, preferably js/src/graph/job-dependency-blocks.ts, with readonly graph/group/layout inputs. No React Flow block nodes, extra workers or effects. layoutResourceGraph/buildResourceElkGraph are out of scope. Existing useAsyncLayout owns async failure/cancellation; do not catch and hide ELK errors or change that lifecycle.

Ordered work:
1. Read dagshund-by22.2 for approved target and numeric gap. Inspect/reuse candidate code and remove any temporary baseline/candidate switch or scratch-only production hooks. Keep only the jobs-layout consumer and helpers it needs.
2. Group job IDs by undirected connectivity of cross-job endpoints, mapping task endpoints with js/src/utils/resource-key.ts::extractTaskNodeParentId (same mapping as collectCrossJobEdges). Ignore intra-job edges for block grouping only, deduplicate pairs, preserve original edges for toFlowEdges. Determine zero-incoming starts from the directed cross-job pairs. Pick first start by (visibleName, stable ID), then sort blocks by that key. Do not alter ELK model order to achieve block ordering; that would risk changing existing task placement.
3. For each ordered block, use existing top-level job positions and dimensions: minX=min(x), minY=min(y), bottom=max(y+height). With cursor=0 initially, set each job to (x-minX, y-minY+cursor), then cursor += bottom-minY+approvedGap. Return a copied positions map. Leave all task entries and all dimensions untouched. No wrap or filling space beside another block.
4. The supported-input algorithm always has starts. If a component has none, leave the entire existing ELK layout unchanged rather than introduce a rootless sort key or partial overlapping placement. This is preservation of old unsupported-input handling only, not cycle support/validation. Do not build cycle-detection features or claim cyclic edges can all point right. Concrete valid-plan counterevidence goes to the coordinator.
5. Add focused pure cases in js/tests/graph/job-dependency-blocks.test.ts and extend js/tests/graph/layout-graph.test.ts as needed. Reuse typed graph fixtures/helpers in existing layout tests and buildGraphEdge, without new assertions/dependencies. Test isolated jobs, empty input, singleton/no-task jobs, chains/branches/joins, multiple starting jobs, a downstream name alphabetically before its start, equal visible names with different IDs, duplicate task-level edges between the same jobs, removed relationships, mixed diff states and dimensions. Supply synthetic ELK geometry to test negative origins, shared minX, full downstream height, exact approved gap and immutability. Verify all task coordinates and job dimensions are unchanged. Test unsupported no-start passthrough as compatibility only. Keep tests behavioral, not snapshots of ELK's incidental absolute coordinates.
6. Cover assembly preservation of node metadata, parentId/extent and edge identity/style. Existing js/tests/components/job-node.test.tsx, flow-canvas.test.tsx, hooks/use-async-layout.test.ts and graph/build-plan-graph.test.ts are regression references; modify only if required by this change. Pure tests cannot substitute for actual ELK/browser evidence because the current test suite documents Worker limitations in Bun tests. Check approved examples in the browser and attach focused observations; final integration handles the combined matrix.

Verification from repository root: prefix commands with direnv exec /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund. Run just test-js; just typecheck-js; bun run --cwd js biome check src/ tests/ (non-mutating); bun run --cwd js build:template. Generated template/CSS must be regenerated, never hand-edited. Use just dev <plan-file> for browser confirmation. Retain failure output and fix only in-scope failures. Follow .agents/guidelines/TYPESCRIPT.md, VISUALIZATION.md and TESTING.md.

description:
Currently the detail panel only shows diff changes — clicking an unchanged node like 'load' shows nothing useful. The panel should display:

1. **Current state** — all fields/config of the resource as they exist (baseline)
2. **Updates** — fields that changed, showing before → after

title: render CLI 1.14 job run outcomes
description:
## Objective

Render Databricks CLI 1.14 `resources.job_runs` semantically in terminal, Markdown, and browser output. The plan action alone is no longer enough: `skip` can mean completed success, a run still in progress, or removal of `on_bundle_deploy`. Preserve the original plan action for counts and detailed exit codes while deriving display semantics from change reasons and remote run state.

## Authoritative CLI 1.14 shapes

Use focused plan vectors based on Databricks CLI v1.14.0. Upstream evidence lives in:

- `acceptance/bundle/resources/job_runs/interrupted_run/output.txt`
- `acceptance/bundle/resources/job_runs/on_bundle_deploy/output.txt`
- `bundle/direct/bundle_plan_test.go`: `TestJobRunFinishedWithoutSuccessIsRecreate`, `TestJobRunInProgressIsSkip`, and `TestJobRunSucceededOutcomeIsNotDrift`

Classify these cases:

1. Completed success: resource action `skip`; remote `result_state` or `state.result_state` is `SUCCESS`; lifecycle is normally `TERMINATED`; `changes.result_state.reason` is normally `remote_already_set`.
2. In progress: resource action `skip`; `changes.result_state.reason == "run in progress"`; remote lifecycle is `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, or `TERMINATING`. CLI 1.14 does not start another run and does not resume waiting for the existing run.
3. Trigger removed: resource action `skip`; a change at `lifecycle`, `lifecycle.triggers`, or `lifecycle.triggers.on_bundle_deploy` has reason `trigger removed`. No run starts.
4. Failed completed run: resource action `recreate`; remote result is `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, or `TIMEDOUT`, or lifecycle is `SKIPPED` or `INTERNAL_ERROR` when no result exists. `remote_state.state.state_message` may explain the outcome. The next deploy re-runs it.
5. Armed every-deploy trigger: resource action `recreate`; lifecycle trigger changes contain non-empty old and new opaque fingerprints under `on_bundle_deploy`. The fingerprints are generated implementation details and must not render.
6. Existing create, ordinary recreate, delete, and older skip shapes remain supported. An unrecognized skip remains the backward-compatible `already ran` fallback.

Extract result state from `remote_state.result_state` first, then `remote_state.state.result_state`. Extract lifecycle and message from `remote_state.state.life_cycle_state` and `remote_state.state.state_message` using safe unknown-value narrowing.

## Required user-facing semantics

Use these exact base phrases:

- create: `runs on deploy`
- ordinary recreate: `re-runs on deploy`
- armed trigger recreate: `runs on every deploy`
- completed-success skip: `already ran successfully`
- unrecognized legacy skip: `already ran`
- in-progress skip: `run still in progress`
- trigger-removal skip: `deploy trigger removed; no run will start`
- delete: `run record will be deleted`

When a recreate has an unsuccessful remote outcome, append `; previous run <OUTCOME>` to either recreate phrase. This also applies when an every-deploy trigger and a failed outcome coexist. Render a non-empty run-level state message as a separate subordinate line/card for in-progress or unsuccessful outcomes. Do not claim task-level detail because plan JSON only carries the run-level message.

Suppress generic field rendering for `result_state`, because it is represented by the semantic outcome and must not be mislabeled as drift. Suppress generated `on_bundle_deploy` fingerprint changes at the three supported lifecycle paths. Only suppress aggregate `lifecycle` or `lifecycle.triggers` entries when their payload is solely the trigger fingerprint container; preserve unrelated lifecycle changes. Preserve all real parameter and configuration changes.

Preserve valid run-page links in Markdown and browser details. Terminal output has never rendered run URLs; do not add terminal URL output in this bead.

## Implementation boundaries

Implement one pure semantic classifier per language and reuse it from every renderer. Do not duplicate condition ladders in terminal, Markdown, badge, and detail components.

Python:

- Extend `JobRunEffect` in `src/dagshund/model.py` with the state needed for classification, preferably `new_state` and `remote_state` to mirror TypeScript.
- Populate those fields in `src/dagshund/merge.py`; do not change target resolution, URL validation, effect ordering, or orphan behavior.
- Put classification and effect-specific visible-change filtering in a focused pure module such as `src/dagshund/job_run_effects.py`.
- Make `src/dagshund/terminal.py` and `src/dagshund/markdown.py` consume the classifier. Keep generic resource field and drift logic unchanged.

TypeScript:

- Keep `normalizePlan` responsible for folding effects and preserving raw state.
- Move action-only wording out of `js/src/utils/normalize-plan.ts` into a focused pure module such as `js/src/utils/job-run-effects.ts`, alongside classification, descriptions, and effect-specific visible-change filtering.
- Use `getUnknownProp` for state inspection. Do not tighten the loose plan Zod schema for these remote fields.
- Make `run-effect-badge.tsx` and `detail-panel/run-effects-section.tsx` consume the shared classifier.

Browser badge policy:

- Exclude delete and trigger-removal effects from the visible badge count.
- If any visible effect fires on deploy, keep the existing green play badge.
- Otherwise, if any visible effect is in progress, render one distinct non-play activity badge using existing palette utilities/styles, with the semantic tooltip.
- Otherwise retain the existing grey completed play badge.
- Keep the tooltip descriptions for all effects when a badge is present. Do not change node diff state.

## Do not implement this elsewhere

This is effect annotation work, not graph topology work. Do not change:

- lateral edge specs, reference specs, resource-key registries, task references, or phantom-node rules
- `build-plan-graph.ts` or `build-resource-graph.ts` effect propagation unless a failing focused test proves an existing propagation bug
- generic `action_config`, generic field-action derivation, structural-diff/drift classification, resource warnings, or resource diff states
- effect target resolution or orphan target behavior
- resource/effect counts, `detect_changes`, dangerous-action classification, or detailed-exit algorithms
- dependencies or the plan schema

The target job must remain unchanged even when a run fires. Effects remain excluded from browser tab counts and diff filters.

## Tests and fixtures

Add `fixtures/job-run-outcome-cases.json` as shared, minimal, hand-authored plan vectors for:

- completed success skip
- in-progress skip
- trigger-removal skip
- failed recreate with state message and run link
- every-deploy recreate with aggregate and leaf fingerprint churn
- every-deploy recreate plus a real parameter change, proving only fingerprint noise is hidden

Test the shared vectors in focused Python and TypeScript classifier tests. Add renderer/component assertions in:

- `tests/test_terminal.py`
- `tests/test_markdown.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`
- `js/tests/components/run-effect-badge.test.tsx`
- `js/tests/components/detail-panel/run-effects-section.test.tsx`

Acceptance assertions:

- completed, in-progress, and trigger-removal skips are visibly distinct
- trigger removal has no play badge
- in-progress has a distinct activity badge
- failed outcome and useful state message render without a drift label
- generated fingerprints never render, while real parameter changes still do
- safe run links remain in Markdown/browser; unsafe URL rejection remains unchanged
- completed/in-progress/trigger-removal-only plans have detailed exit 0
- failed/every-deploy recreate-only plans have detailed exit 2
- resource and run summary counts remain action-based and unchanged
- parent job diff state and browser tab/filter counts remain unchanged

Do not create a new stateful or supervised golden workflow and do not modify `fixtures/golden/job-runs/before` or `after` to manufacture these states. The existing real `job-runs` golden remains integration evidence for create, ordinary recreate, delete, completed-success skip, links, counts, and effect-only exit 2. If its expected generated output changes because completed-success wording improves, regenerate with `nix develop --command just gen-expected job-runs`; never hand-edit generated golden output. Update README job-run wording to match the final semantics.

title: Build graph model: Plan to React Flow nodes and edges
description:
Transform a parsed Plan (from parser/) into React Flow-compatible nodes and edges. All pure functions, no React code.

WHAT EXISTS:
- Plan type with record of PlanEntry (keyed by resource path string like 'resources.jobs.etl_pipeline')
- Each PlanEntry has: id, depends_on, action, changes, new_state, remote_state
- DiffState type: added | removed | modified | unchanged
- mapActionToDiffState function in parser/map-diff-state.ts
- Two real fixtures: sample-plan.json (all creates) and mixed-plan.json (updates/skips/removals)

KEY INSIGHT — THE DATA HAS THREE LEVELS:
1. Resource level: top-level plan entries keyed like 'resources.jobs.etl_pipeline'. Each has an action (create/update/delete/skip).
2. Task level: inside new_state.value.tasks, each task has task_key, depends_on (array of {task_key}), notebook_task, etc. These form the actual DAG the user wants to see.
3. Change level: the 'changes' record has keys like 'tasks[task_key=extract].notebook_task.notebook_path' with per-field actions (update/skip/delete). This tells us WHICH tasks and fields changed.

THE GRAPH MODEL MUST:
- Extract tasks from new_state.value.tasks as individual graph nodes
- Build edges from each task's depends_on array (task_key references)
- Determine each task's DiffState by checking the changes record:
  - If changes has 'tasks[task_key=X]' with action=update and only a 'new' field (no 'old') → added
  - If changes has 'tasks[task_key=X]' with action=update and only an 'old' field (no 'new') → removed
  - If changes has 'tasks[task_key=X].some.field' with action=update → modified
  - If all changes for task X are action=skip → unchanged
  - If the resource-level action is 'create' → all tasks are added
- Also produce a job-level metadata node showing the resource itself (name, triggers, etc.) — this is context, not part of the task DAG edges
- Handle multiple jobs in the plan (each is a separate sub-graph)

WHAT TO BUILD in src/graph/:
1. Graph types in src/types/graph-types.ts:
   - GraphNode: id, label, nodeKind ('job' | 'task'), diffState, resourceKey, taskKey?, raw data ref
   - GraphEdge: id, source, target, label?
   - PlanGraph: { readonly nodes: readonly GraphNode[], readonly edges: readonly GraphEdge[] }
2. extractTaskNodes(resourceKey: string, entry: PlanEntry) → readonly GraphNode[]
   - Dig into new_state.value.tasks, create a node per task
   - Compute diffState per task from the changes record

title: Click task → slide-in detail panel showing changes
description:
When a user clicks a task node, a detail panel slides in from the right side showing all changes for that task.

### Behavior
- Click a task node → panel slides in from the right (~350-400px wide)
- Panel shows: task name, diff state badge, and a list of all changes
- Each change entry shows: field path, old value, new value, action type
- Click outside panel or click an X button → panel closes
- Clicking a different task updates the panel contents
- Clicking a job container node could show job-level changes

### Data
The `changes` field is already computed and attached to each node's data (`DagNodeData.changes`). It's a `Record<string, ChangeDesc>` where ChangeDesc has old/new values and action.

- `src/App.tsx` — add state for selected node, render panel conditionally
- `src/hooks/use-selected-node.ts` — optional hook to manage selection state
- `src/components/index.ts` — barrel export

### Styling
Dark theme consistent with existing zinc-950 background. Panel should have a subtle border-left separator. Changes displayed in a clean diff-like format.

title: Filter unchanged and wheel-only changes out of plan review
description:
Large PR plan outputs are dominated by unchanged resources and repeated routine wheel artifact updates. Reviewers need a focused non-wheel change view in terminal, Markdown CI output, and generated HTML, including nested jobs and pipelines, without losing awareness of which wheels are being deployed.

Agreed behavior: wheel suppression changes the effective diff consistently throughout the hierarchy, rather than merely hiding task fields or changing task styling. Wheel-only items become effectively unchanged while suppression is enabled. Mixed items retain their non-wheel differences. Wheel information is summarized separately once per plan, rather than repeated per task or job. Original plan data remains available for the full unsuppressed view.

Reuse existing controls: --suppress-wheel-updates and the HTML wheel-suppression toggle, combined with existing status/unchanged filters. No new combined filter or CLI flags are needed. The intended CI command is dagshund plan.json -c --suppress-wheel-updates; -c already aliases --changes-only.
design:
Agreed presentation and filtering contract

1. Suppression off: preserve existing full diff behavior. Wheel-only resources count as modified, and wheel differences appear inline. Existing status filters continue to work normally.
2. Suppression on: routine wheel churn does not contribute to effective change classification. Apply this consistently to tasks, resources, parent jobs and other containers, including supported nested job and pipeline shapes. A parent must not remain modified solely because of suppressed descendant wheel changes; its own substantive differences and substantive descendant differences still count.
3. Every presentation uses the same effective diff: node styling, badges, summary/filter counts, status filtering, detail-panel differences, changed-task lists, and terminal/Markdown resource sections. Do not leave suppressed task changes listed as changes in parent details.
4. Existing -c/--changes-only, -m/--modified, and -f status:modified must use the wheel-suppressed classification when suppression is enabled. With suppression alone, wheel-only items may remain visible as unchanged. With suppression plus changes-only, unchanged and wheel-only items are excluded from review results. Any HTML ancestors retained solely for navigation are neutral context, not reported changes.
5. Preserve real additions/removals, genuine drift, topology changes, and substantive dependency/resource differences. Suppression must not conceal resource/task creation or deletion just because wheels are involved. Verify the precise routine-churn boundary against representative real shapes; wheel additions/removals, distribution swaps, extras changes, and meaningful compatibility changes are not routine rebuild noise.

Separate wheel summary

Replace per-job wheel-updated lines with one plan-level Wheel updates section while suppression is enabled, consistently in terminal, Markdown, and HTML. Suppress repetition, not information that wheels changed. Each distinct distribution plus old/new version transition appears once; different transitions for the same distribution remain separate. Show accurate affected-carrier/resource counts where appropriate, without labeling pipeline/environment carriers as tasks. Account for supported same-version artifact-path updates without inventing a version transition.

The wheel summary survives changes-only filtering, including updates belonging to wheel-only resources that no longer appear in individual review sections. It is separate from non-wheel change counts and must not make those resources count as modified. Exact formatting and interaction details may follow existing output conventions; no new control is required. Behavior with additional explicit search/type filters should be made coherent during implementation.

Output examples, schematic rather than a formatting redesign:
- Mixed plan: show the actual non-wheel resource differences, a non-wheel change count, then Wheel updates listing each distinct transition once across affected jobs/tasks.
- Only wheel updates: No non-wheel changes, followed by Wheel updates. Do not claim No changes or omit the wheel information.
- Truly unchanged plan: No changes, with no empty wheel section.

HTML uses the same semantics: a plan-level wheel summary, effective status/filter/count/detail behavior, and full original differences restored when suppression is switched off. Disabling CLI suppression restores ordinary full wheel diffs on the next invocation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Suppression consistently treats wheel-only items and their otherwise unchanged parent containers as effectively unchanged in HTML, Markdown, and terminal output.
- [x] Mixed resources retain every non-wheel difference, while genuine additions/removals, drift, topology changes, and substantive dependency changes remain reviewable.
- [x] Existing status controls (-c, -m, -f status:modified, and HTML unchanged/status filtering) consume the effective classification; suppression plus changes-only removes unchanged/wheel-only review noise without a new filter or flag.
- [x] Styles, badges, summary/filter counts, parent detail panels, and changed-task lists agree; no suppressed wheel-only task remains listed as a substantive parent change.
- [x] Suppression produces a separate deduplicated plan-level wheel summary instead of per-job wheel-updated lines. Distinct transitions remain distinguishable and affected-carrier counts are accurate.
- [x] The wheel summary remains visible with changes-only even when all individual wheel-only resources are filtered out. Wheel-only plans say No non-wheel changes and still report wheel updates; truly unchanged plans say No changes.
- [x] Suppression off preserves/restores full original differences and statuses; HTML retains the full plan for reversible toggling.
- [x] Representative regression cases cover nested jobs, pipelines, classic/serverless carriers, wheel-only and mixed changes, parent propagation, filters/counts/details, and the genuine-change boundary across Python and TypeScript behavior.
- [x] Any private user fixture used for investigation remains out of Git; committed regression cases must be independently safe/sanitized.
notes: Behavior agreed with the user in discussion. Current implementation suppresses task fields/styles but leaves parent jobs modified and parent detail lists noisy; terminal/Markdown report classification also remains based on unsuppressed actions. The original per-job wheel-updated line was a summarization workaround, not a requirement to retain that placement. The user still wants awareness of wheel deployment, so the agreed replacement is a separate plan-level wheel summary, not silent removal. A private fixture may be supplied later; do not request or use it yet, and never commit it. This update records the agreement only; implementation has not started.
